title: Temporal Expert-Based Reward Learning for Inverse Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Learning reward functions from expert demonstrations removes the need for manual reward engineering in reinforcement learning applied to robotic manipulation. Existing methods, however, require trajectory quality annotations, episode success labels, or produce implicit rewards that are difficult to inspect. This paper presents TEXB-IRL (Temporal EXpert-Based reward learning for Inverse Reinforcement Learning), which learns a dense neural reward function directly from unlabeled expert demonstrations. TEXB-IRL exploits intra-trajectory temporal ordering through two complementary objectives: a temporal consistency loss that enforces monotonically increasing reward along expert trajectories, and an expert-agent separation loss that anchors the reward scale. The policy is optimized with PPO over the learned reward. Preliminary experiments in simulation with the PAL TIAGo++ robot show competitive results against state of the art algorithms.

title: Chinese cyberbullying detection via multi-feature prompt learning
abstract: Most existing research on cyberbullying detection reduces the task to comment-level hate speech classification, overlooking its collective, event-driven, and dynamic nature. To address this limitation, we propose CDMPL, a multi-feature prompt learning framework for Chinese cyberbullying incident detection. CDMPL integrates textual features (semantic summaries generated by large language models) with temporal features (temporal behavioral patterns captured by a Dynamic Attention Truncation mechanism and an Autoformer-based time series encoder). These fused features are reformulated as a masked language modeling task, enhancing interpretability and robustness. We evaluate CDMPL on the only publicly available Chinese incident-level dataset, consisting of 86 cyberbullying and 109 non-cyberbullying events. Under a 15-shot setting, CDMPL achieves 84.79% accuracy and 84.05% F1-score, exceeding state-of-the-art large language models such as Doubao (71.91% F1) and ChatGPT-4o (70.06% F1) by more than 12%. Ablation studies further demonstrate the necessity of jointly modeling semantic and temporal features. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic study of Chinese incident-level cyberbullying detection, providing methodological and empirical advances for early detection and governance.

title: Structural Cost Optimization of Reinforced Concrete Frames Using Metaheuristic Algorithms and Commercial Software APIs
abstract: This paper presents a computational methodology for the cost optimization of three-dimensional reinforced concrete building frames, integrating metaheuristic optimization algorithms with the ETABS structural analysis software API.The framework minimizes the total structural cost of concrete, reinforcing steel, and formwork while complying with ACI 318-19 and applicable seismic design provisions.Three algorithms were implemented and compared under an equivalent computational budget -Real-Coded Genetic Algorithm (RCGA), Discrete Variable Genetic Algorithm (DVGA), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO)together with dedicated genetic algorithms for beam and column reinforcement detailing.RCGA exhibited the most favorable convergence and produced the minimum-cost design, which achieved a 9.47% cost reduction relative to a conventional design representative of standard engineering practice.The results indicate that the proposed methodology is an effective computational tool for improving the economic efficiency of reinforced concrete frame design.

title: Wavefront phase prediction in atmospheric turbulence using speckle-based optical next generation reservoir computing
abstract: In this work, we propose a method for wavefront phase prediction in atmospheric turbulence using speckle-based optical next-generation reservoir computing (NGRC). The wavefront state is represented by Zernike coefficients, and the coefficients at two adjacent time steps are used as delayed inputs and encoded onto a spatial light modulator. A random scattering medium then maps the modulated optical field into high-dimensional speckle intensity patterns, which are recorded by a camera and used as nonlinear reservoir states. Only a linear readout layer is trained using Tikhonov regularization to predict future wavefront phases. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves effective prediction over prediction horizons h=2–6 under five turbulence strengths and reduces the wavefront error by at least 53.2% compared with the non-predictive baseline. Compared with the Kalman filter and the ConvLSTM model, optical NGRC achieves lower prediction errors while using only two input steps and without repeated epoch-based training. The long-term autoregressive prediction further reveals that optical NGRC better preserves the dominant spectral and statistical characteristics of the reference sequence, demonstrating its effectiveness in capturing the essential dynamical features of turbulent wavefront evolution.

title: Provably secure federated learning with ECCDH-based group key agreement for enhanced privacy in collaborative model training
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) facilitates collaborative training of models without exchanging any data, thereby ensuring data locality. However, the exchange of local model updates is still susceptible to attacks such as gradient inference, model reconstruction, man-in-the-middle, replay, and tampering, which create considerable privacy and security concerns. In this paper, we propose a framework for secure federated learning by combining a decentralized group key establishment scheme using ECCDH, SHA-256 based key derivation, cryptographically secure PRNG-based additive masking, and ECDSA authentication for protecting local model updates in a collaborative training process. While existing schemes require key management infrastructure, trusted third parties, or homomorphic/hyperencryption/multi-party computation techniques, our scheme allows clients to establish a common cryptographic seed in a collaborative fashion.The derived seeds are converted into synchronized masking vectors through the utilization of a secure PRNG, enabling the clients to mask their local models' updates while still maintaining compatibility with the standard FedAvg aggregation algorithm. Additionally, the use of SHA-256 and ECDSA guarantees message integrity, client authentication, and replay protection before performing the aggregation process. The formal security model and theorem prove the security properties of confidentiality, integrity, authentication, replay resistance, forward secrecy, and collusion resistance of the proposed scheme under the probabilistic polynomial-time (PPT) adversary under the hardness assumption of the ECDLP and CDH problems. The experimental study performed on five benchmark data sets (i.e., Iris, Breast Cancer, Wine, Diabetes, and Prostate Cancer) shows that the proposed framework maintains similar predictive performance as the conventional federated learning while incurring minimal overhead costs. Hence, the findings show that the proposed ECCDH-based secure aggregation framework provides an efficient and scalable way of federated learning without the use of any trusted third party.

title: Generative Diffusion Surrogates with Analytical Variance Schedule
abstract: Stochastic transport describes physical systems in which an initially structured distribution spreads under unresolved forcing, scattering, or heterogeneous media. Useful surrogates for such systems should be probabilistic, time-resolved, and able to represent non-Gaussian distributional structure. Generative diffusion models, which corrupt data with Gaussian noise and learn a reverse flow back to structured states, have these properties. Their noise schedules, however, are usually chosen heuristically: image and audio generation---the canonical use cases---provide no physical clock. In transport, by contrast, the variance, or mean-square displacement, is often known from macroscopic theory or empirical scaling even when the full distribution is not. Here we prescribe the forward noising rate as the time derivative of this variance, turning generative time into a calibrated transport clock. The variance path is enforced by construction, while the learned score field represents how non-Gaussian structure inherited from entrance data is smoothed along that path, requiring no intermediate-time physical transport data. For ballistic-to-diffusive transport in turbulent plasmas, the surrogate matches test-particle distributions, reproduces the laboratory-measured variance scale, and tracks the simulated kurtosis evolution without schedule tuning, enabling calibrated emulation and likelihood-based inference.

title: Towards Generalizable Visually Grounded Exploration of Household Devices
abstract: Recent advancements in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities in static visual recognition and high-level semantic reasoning. However, current embodied exploration paradigms still heavily rely on imitation learning from human-annotated trajectories, which severely limits agents' generalization ability. The key bottleneck of realizing general autonomous embodied agents lies in Generalizable Visually Grounded Exploration: the ability to operate novel devices without manuals or specific training by actively grounding abstract world knowledge into fine-grained visual affordances. Yet, existing benchmarks fail to evaluate this capability: they generally rely on explicit documents and annotated trajectories, neglecting the dynamic Hypothesis-Interaction-Refinement process essential for functional device operation. To bridge this gap, we introduce VGEBench, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate the generalizable visually grounded exploration capabilities of VLMs. Unlike static datasets, we construct a Logic-Driven State Machine framework. This framework simulates multi-turn interaction loops, compelling agents to achieve goals by active visual perception and feedback-driven correction. Experimental results demonstrate that existing VLMs face significant challenges in translating semantic knowledge into physical execution and maintaining long-horizon state tracking.

title: Restrict, Don't Retrain: Inference-Time VLM Guidance for Zero-Shot Aerial Segmentation
abstract: Global welfare often depends on the correct interpretation of aerial and satellite imagery. Acting on such imagery (mapping flooded ground, crop extent, or damaged infrastructure) demands pixel-level segmentation to ensure perfect class localization. Pretrained general foundation models, when applied directly, often miss important features and cannot always find all the classes belonging to a given scene, overlooking smaller objects that matter most. We use a single consumer-grade GPU running a vision-language model (VLM) to supply this missing guidance, improving segmentation while producing structured, auditable evidence that drives the result and can be inspected on its own. We fuse three approaches: the frozen foundation model that labels every pixel, and two queries to a VLM, one to choose the classes that matter, and one to locate the small objects the base model misses. Evaluating across four aerial datasets, we see consistent gains at each stage where the base model is competent.

title: ChainSWE: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Multi-Bug Software Maintenance
abstract: Language model (LM) agents are increasingly deployed to maintain codebases over extended periods, fixing streams of related defects while carrying context from one fix to the next. Yet existing software engineering (SWE) benchmarks evaluate models one bug at a time: the repository is reset, the codebase is re-read, and a single self-contained issue is graded in isolation. This setting collapses a continuous maintenance workflow into a series of independent sessions, ignoring the cumulative dependencies that make real-world bug fixing challenging. To bridge this gap, we introduce ChainSWE, the first benchmark for evaluating agents on sequential, dependent bug fixes within a shared codebase. We collect chronological chains of 304 issues across 54 Python projects, mined from six SWE-bench-family datasets. Our evaluation across a range of agents and models reveals a consistent performance drop by up to 70% as the chain length increases.

To bridge this gap, we introduce ChainSWE, the first benchmark for evaluating agents on sequential, dependent bug fixes within a shared codebase. We collect chronological chains of 304 issues across 54 Python projects, mined from six SWE-bench-family datasets. Our evaluation across a range of agents and models reveals a consistent performance drop by up to 70% as the chain length increases.

title: Detecting breast carcinoma metastasis on whole-slide images by partially subsampled multiple instance learning
abstract: Breast cancer is the most prevalent cancer in women worldwide. Histopathology image analysis serves as the gold standard for cancer diagnosis. In this regard, whole-slide imaging (WSI), a revolutionary technology in digital pathology, allows for ultrahigh-resolution tissue analysis. Despite its promise, WSI analysis faces significant computational challenges due to its massive data size and tissue heterogeneity. To address this issue, we present a Gaussian mixture based multiple instance learning (MIL) framework for WSI analysis with partially subsampled instances. Our approach models a WSI as a bag of instances (i.e., randomly cropped subimages), leveraging a bag-based maximum likelihood estimator (BMLE) to predict metastases. Furthermore, we introduce a subsampling-based maximum likelihood estimator (SMLE) to refine predictions by selectively labeling a subset of instances. Extensive evaluations of the breast carcinoma metastasis prediction demonstrate that BMLE surpasses state-of-the-art methods, while the SMLE further improves the prediction accuracy at both bag and instance levels. We find that our method is fairly robust against various plausible model misspecifications. Theoretical analyses and simulation studies validate the performance and robustness of our methods.

title: Unpaired Imaging–Histopathology Alignment for Prostate Cancer Grading
abstract: Prostate cancer treatment depends on accurate assessment of tumour aggressiveness, established through histopathologic examination using the International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) Grade Group system. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and micro-ultrasound (micro-US) provide clinically useful information before and during biopsy, respectively, but do not directly capture the microscopic tissue architecture that defines tumour grade. Although histopathology models encode these features, transferring their knowledge to imaging models is difficult because matched, spatially registered datasets are scarce. This thesis develops and evaluates an unpaired representation learning framework that uses histopathology to improve prostate cancer assessment from medical imaging. A histopathology model first generates representations of whole-slide prostate biopsies. Using ISUP Grade Group as a shared clinical anchor, an imaging encoder is trained with a margin-based triplet loss to align its representations with same-grade histopathology representations and separate them from those of different grades. The framework requires neither patient correspondence nor spatial registration, and histopathology is used only during training. The framework was first evaluated for MRI prediction across three categories: ISUP Grade Groups 0-1, 2-3, and 4-5. Histopathology alignment increased overall area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) from 72.3% to 81.1% and increased AUROC for Grade Groups 4-5 from 56.7% to 85.0%. Sensitivity increased from 82.0% to 94.8% at 40% specificity and from 72.7% to 84.3% at 60% specificity. The framework was then adapted for cancer detection and weakly supervised localization in micro-US by combining histopathology alignment with a segmentation objective. Compared with the strongest baseline, sensitivity to higher-grade disease (Grade Group greater than or equal to 3) increased from 82.5% to 86.0% at 60% specificity. Overall AUROC increased from 77.9% to 78.4%, while mean entropy within the biopsy region decreased from 7.32 to 6.78, indicating more decisive predictions. Together, these studies demonstrate that knowledge of prostate cancer grade can be transferred from histopathology to imaging encoders without paired datasets. By improving imaging-based assessment of tumour aggressiveness without requiring histopathology at deployment, the proposed framework could strengthen risk stratification from imaging alone, support earlier identification of high-risk disease, and help guide biopsy targeting and treatment decisions.

title: The hidden barrier to AI success: Trusted data foundations
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has reached a critical inflection point in financial services. Despite its extraordinary promise, most AI initiatives in post-trade operations struggle to move beyond experimentation. This paper sets out to address that gap within post-trade operations, where accuracy, predictability, and control are non-negotiable. It examines why AI initiatives stall, identifies the conditions required for scalable adoption, and outlines how companies can move from isolated pilots to repeatable, production-grade deployment. Readers will gain a clear understanding of where AI adds genuine value, particularly across exceptions management, reconciliation, allocations, and trade enrichment. The paper also introduces a best practice centred on data readiness, governance, and decision transparency, ensuring every AI-driven outcome is traceable and controlled. By the end, readers will be equipped with practical guidance to define high-value use cases, strengthen data foundations, and implement AI in a way that delivers measurable, compliant, and sustainable results across post-trade functions. This article is also included in The Business & Management Collection which can be accessed at https://hstalks.com/business/.

title: FUTURE TRENDS IN COMPUTER TECHNOLOGY: EMERGING INNOVATIONS, CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES
abstract: Computer technology is entering a period of rapid transformation in which artificial intelligence, generative AI, quantum computing, edge computing, cloud-native systems, the Internet of Things, advanced robotics, 6G communications, digital twins, neuromorphic computing, and sustainable computing are converging. The future computer is increasingly expected to be intelligent, distributed, secure, energy-efficient, autonomous, and capable of interacting naturally with humans and the physical environment. This research article presents a structured review of major future trends in computer technology and examines their potential applications, opportunities, limitations, and research challenges. The study synthesizes established academic and institutional literature to identify how emerging technologies may reshape computing architectures, software development, cybersecurity, healthcare, education, finance, manufacturing, agriculture, transportation, and smart cities. Particular attention is given to the transition from centralized cloud computing toward hybrid cloud-edge environments; the integration of AI into software and infrastructure; the emergence of quantum and neuromorphic approaches for specialized workloads; privacy-preserving machine learning; post-quantum security; and green computing. The article argues that future progress will depend not only on computational performance but also on trustworthiness, interoperability, governance, affordability, energy efficiency, human-centered design, and responsible innovation. The findings provide a consolidated research agenda for scholars and practitioners interested in next-generation computer technology.

title: Bigger, Better, or Just Bigger: A Critical Survey Review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of scaling laws and compute as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Cave Lion: A Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Cave Lion Hunting Strategies
abstract: This paper introduces Cave Lion, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting strategies employed by cave lions. The algorithm leverages concepts such as ambushing, coordinated movement, and resource prioritization, mimicking the intelligent behavior of these apex predators. Cave Lion utilizes a population-based approach, employing a dynamic agent representation and a novel adaptive inertia weight mechanism. The algorithm's core components include a virtual environment simulation, agent movement rules, and a scoring function that evaluates the fitness of each agent based on its proximity to the optimal solution. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the algorithm's mechanics, including the probability of agent movement, the update rules for agent positions, and the calculation of the fitness score. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a set of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The results indicate that Cave Lion provides a competitive alternative to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems requiring spatial reasoning and coordinated decision-making. The key parameters and their influence on the algorithm's performance are analyzed, offering insights into the algorithm's tuning and potential improvements. Keywords: Metaheuristic Optimization, Cave Lion, Hunting Strategies, Population-Based Algorithm, Adaptive Inertia Weight, Spatial Optimization.

title: Causal Inference on Streaming Data with Online Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper explores the application of online Bayesian networks for causal inference in streaming data environments. Traditional Bayesian network approaches often require the entire dataset to be available before model learning and inference can be performed, which is impractical for continuous data streams. This work introduces a novel algorithm for updating an online Bayesian network in real-time, incorporating new observations while preserving the integrity of the causal model. The core of the approach lies in dynamically adjusting network parameters based on incoming data, enabling continuous causal discovery and inference within evolving systems. This capability is crucial for scenarios where the underlying causal relationships are not static but rather fluctuate over time, such as dynamic social networks, evolving biological systems, and real-time economic forecasting. The methodology presented offers a significant advancement in causal inference techniques, moving beyond static models to a more adaptive and robust framework.

title: 基于自适应的神经符号模型的学习与推理
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for learning and reasoning based on adaptive neural-symbolic models. Traditional approaches often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the model's ability to effectively tackle complex reasoning tasks. Our proposed method dynamically adjusts the parameters of the neural symbol components, enabling a more flexible and efficient learning process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments on a variety of reasoning benchmarks, showcasing significant improvements in accuracy and speed compared to existing techniques. The core mechanism focuses on continuous parameter optimization to enhance the model's understanding and inference capabilities. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance, highlighting its advantages and limitations.

title: Quantum Topological Optimization for Complex Systems
abstract: Quantum topological optimization offers a novel approach to solving complex optimization problems by leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics. This paper introduces a framework based on quantum entanglement and topological structure, demonstrating its potential for optimizing intricate systems. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the topology of a system, guided by quantum computations, to achieve optimal solutions. The core mechanism involves manipulating the system's structure through quantum entanglement, resulting in a significant improvement over traditional optimization techniques. This research explores the feasibility of this approach in a specific case study – optimizing a network topology – highlighting the potential for transformative advancements in various fields.

title: Multi-Modal Information Fusion via Evolutionary Probabilistic Graphical Models
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to multi-modal information fusion utilizing an evolutionary algorithm applied to probabilistic graphical models. The core idea is to automate the learning and optimization of fusion structures and parameters within these models, specifically focusing on Bayesian Networks and Markov Networks. We propose a framework where a genetic algorithm iteratively evolves the structure and parameters of a chosen graphical model, guided by a fitness function that quantifies the quality of the fusion – typically measured by improved joint probability estimation or predictive accuracy. The algorithm's ability to explore the complex parameter space of these models is key to discovering optimal fusion configurations that may not be readily apparent through traditional manual design. This work addresses the limitations of manual design in multi-modal fusion by providing an automated and adaptive solution. The resulting model represents a significant advancement in the field, offering a robust and scalable method for integrating diverse data sources.

abstract: Quantum algorithms are increasingly crucial for complex computations, and efficient implementation is vital for practical applications. This paper presents a novel quantum algorithm, termed "Adaptive Topology Control Quantum Algorithm" (ATCAQA), which leverages quantum entanglement and topological structure to enhance algorithm complexity and efficiency. The core of ATCAQA is a dynamic mapping and manipulation of the quantum state, guided by entanglement, to achieve complex computational tasks. We detail the algorithm's design, the underlying mathematical principles, and its potential advantages over existing approaches. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future research directions for this innovative quantum algorithm.

title: Causal Discovery via Graph Generative Adversarial Networks
abstract: Discovering causal relationships from observational data is a fundamental problem in machine learning and statistics. Traditional causal discovery methods often rely on strong assumptions or require extensive prior knowledge. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing Graph Generative Adversarial Networks (GGANs) to address this challenge. The core idea is to train a GGAN to generate synthetic data that conforms to a hypothesized causal graph. The generator network learns to produce data consistent with the graph's structure, while the discriminator network evaluates the generated data against the graph's causal relationships. Through this adversarial training process, the GGAN effectively learns and represents the underlying causal structure. This approach offers a flexible and data-driven method for causal discovery, particularly beneficial when direct causal inference is difficult or impossible. The success of this method hinges on the quality of the initial hypothesized causal graph, which can be iteratively refined through the learning process. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this approach and demonstrate its potential through a conceptual framework.

title: ## Bongo: A Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of Bongos
abstract: This paper introduces Bongo, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of bongos, a species of African antelope. Bongos exhibit a complex and adaptable strategy for locating food resources, characterized by exploration, exploitation, and a dynamic adjustment of search patterns. Bongo leverages these principles to create a new optimization algorithm suitable for a wide range of problems. The algorithm employs a multi-dimensional search space, utilizing a modified roulette wheel selection mechanism combined with a novel "resonance" component that mimics the bongos' ability to detect and respond to subtle environmental cues. We present the algorithm's design, its core principles, and demonstrate its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and conceptual examples. The key innovations of Bongo lie in its dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation balance and the resonance mechanism, which enhances its ability to escape local optima. The algorithm's performance is evaluated conceptually, illustrating its potential advantages over traditional metaheuristic approaches. Future research directions, including implementation and experimental validation, are also discussed.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Metamorphic Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum computing to enhance metamorphic optimization, a challenging problem for complex optimization. We propose a novel quantum-enhanced metamorphic optimization technique predicated on leveraging quantum properties to accelerate the optimization process and improve robustness. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with the complexity of these problems, necessitating computationally intensive approaches. This work explores the potential of quantum computing to address these limitations, aiming to achieve substantial improvements in optimization speed and solution quality. We detail the core mechanism, the rationale behind the quantum enhancement, and the expected results through analysis and simulation. The core claim of this study is that implementing a quantum-enhanced metamorphic optimization technique results in improved robustness and accelerated convergence.

title: The Fourth Paradigm at Work: A Historical Development Review of Machine Learning for Scientific Discovery
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Machine Learning for Scientific Discovery in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of AI for science and discovery as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Detecting Program Cycles through Power Consumption
abstract: Kryptografické algoritmy na mřížkách využívají techniku zvanou rejection sampling, aby zajistily, že vygenerované podpisy budou odpovídat danému náhodnému rozdělení. Tato technika způsobuje cykly, ve kterých se vykoná náhodný počet iterací. Z tohoto důvodu pak naměřené průběhy spotřeby těchto algoritmů nejsou zarovnané v čase, což ztěžuje analýzu postranních kanálů. V této práci navrhujeme metodu na identifikaci cyklů v průbězích spotřeby, určení počtu jejich iterací a nalezení začátků jednotlivých iterací každého cyklu. Tato metoda vychází z Rapid Alignment Method a mohla by umožnit zarovnání průběhů spotřeby u algoritmů, které využívají rejection sampling, a pomoci automatizovat útoky Simple Power Analysis.

title: Centre of Gravity Based Fuzzy Logic Control for Autoclave Pressure Stabilisation with Internet of Things Monitoring
abstract: General Background Autoclave sterilization relies on pressurized steam, making stable pressure and temperature important process parameters. Specific Background A previous Arduino and Internet of Things autoclave used binary on-off heater regulation, which may generate repeated switching around the setpoint because stored thermal energy can continue raising pressure after the heater is switched off. Knowledge Gap The existing system therefore requires a nonbinary regulation structure capable of adjusting heating intensity according to pressure conditions rather than relying solely on on-off switching. Aims This study develops a Mamdani fuzzy logic controller using normalized pressure error and change of error as inputs and heater duty cycle as the output obtained through Center of Gravity defuzzification. Results Five linguistic sets for each variable generated 25 fuzzy rules. Static inference at zero change of error produced approximately 2.67–3.04% output above the setpoint, 20% at the setpoint, and 32.59–75.00% below the setpoint, demonstrating progressively adjusted heating action. Novelty The proposed configuration extends the existing Arduino and Internet of Things autoclave architecture by integrating normalized error, Mamdani inference, Center of Gravity defuzzification, and time-proportional heater operation. Implications The structure provides a basis for smoother pressure regulation and traceable monitoring, but hardware testing remains necessary before claims regarding overshoot, settling time, relay switching, or energy consumption can be established. Highlights: Twenty five IF THEN rules map normalized pressure error and error change to duty cycle. Above setpoint conditions yielded COG outputs near 2.7–3.0%, whereas lower pressures required 32.59–75.00%. Dynamic hardware validation remains necessary before overshoot, settling time, switching, or energy claims. Keywords: Autoclave, Center of Gravity, Fuzzy Logic Control, Internet of Things, Pressure Control

title: Wine and dine with AI
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated into hospitality and wine service, its ability to support customer satisfaction in high-contact settings remains unclear. The purpose of this multiphase mixed methods study was to identify the drivers of customer satisfaction in fine-dining wine service, examine whether AI-supported wine recommendation technologies are perceived as capable of aligning with those drivers, explore differences across customer groups, and incorporate industry professionals' perspectives on the potential role of AI in wine service. Survey data from 154 participants were analyzed to examine satisfaction drivers, perceived AI capabilities, demographic differences, and preferences for AI-supported service. Open-ended survey responses and interviews with five wine service professionals provided qualitative perspectives that were integrated with quantitative findings through triangulation. Customers placed the greatest importance on wine quality and value, tailored recommendations, and accessible information. Perceived AI capability ratings exceeded corresponding satisfaction ratings across all 11 measures, yet 67.6% of participants disagreed that they would prefer an AI-based tool over a human or sommelier. Qualitative customer findings emphasized personalization, knowledgeable guidance, and meaningful interaction. The five industry professionals interviewed identified there were some opportunities for AI assistance, but emphasized that responsiveness, expertise, and human connection were central to effective wine service. Triangulation revealed that customers were more consistent in what they valued than in what they believed AI could provide; perceived AI capability did not necessarily translate into preference for AI; and acceptance of AI-supported wine service depended in part on preserving human interaction and the fine-dining experience. The findings suggest that AI-supported wine recommendation technologies may be most appropriately implemented as optional decision-support tools that translate customer preferences into personalized guidance, offer multiple pathways to a satisfying wine decision, and complement human expertise without disrupting the dining experience.

title: From Masks to Biomarkers: A Pathology-Style Tool with Novel Oracle-Bounded Model Fusion
abstract: Automated nucleus segmentation is central to quantitative pathology, yet even high-performing deep learning models remain inconsistent across tissue regions with different staining, cell density, and boundary ambiguity.This study presents a pathology-style region-of-interest analysis tool and a model-fusion framework for improving the reliability and interpretability of nucleus segmentation.The tool allows users to inspect segmentation overlays and export standardized measurements such as nucleus area, nearest-neighbor distance, local density, and clustering summaries.Model performance was evaluated on MoNuSeg using CellViT, CellViT++, and CellSAM.To determine whether global performance rankings conceal useful regional specialization, model predictions were compared within non-overlapping 64 × 64 regions using a ground-truth-guided oracle analysis.The reconstructed oracle mask reached a Dice score of 0.8540, approximately 0.028 above the strongest individual model.Oracle winners were distributed across CellViT, CellViT++, and CellSAM at 39.5%, 35.7%, and 24.8%, respectively, demonstrating that all three models contributed meaningful local strengths despite substantial differences in their overall performance.Two practical fusion strategies were also evaluated.Majority voting reached a Dice score of 0.8146 and underperformed the strongest individual model because rigid consensus removed valid detections supported by only one model.In contrast, probabilistic distillation produced a compact student model with a Dice score of 0.8250, preserving performance near the strongest teacher while requiring only one model at inference.Together, the oracle analysis and probabilistic distillation provide a possible approach for combining models with complementary local strengths by first identifying the available benefit and then transferring multi-model information into a single network.These findings show that model disagreement contains structured and scientifically useful information that is obscured by aggregate performance metrics.The study establishes measurable headroom for adaptive local model selection and provides a foundation for more reliable and computationally practical pathology-style biomarker workflows.

title: A generative label-explanation-driven discriminative semantic-structure fusion for relation extraction
abstract: Relation extraction identifies semantic relations between entities from unstructured text and is a core task in information extraction. Existing methods still struggle to generalize in complex contexts, long tail relation types, and cross domain settings, largely because single level modeling cannot fully capture cross level dependencies and complementary cues. To address this issue, a generative label explanation driven discriminative semantic structure fusion framework for relation extraction is proposed, leveraging a synergistic paradigm of generative semantic augmentation and discriminative representation learning to improve relation classification. The proposed method follows a collaborative paradigm of generative semantic enhancement and discriminative representation learning. Specifically, large language models are leveraged to augment relation instances and generate label explanations, which explicitly inject label semantic priors and mitigate data sparsity and class imbalance. In the discriminative stage, hierarchical semantic structures are modeled at the word level via mask-aware prompting, at the phrase level via planar semantics with spatial dependency modeling, and at the sentence level via a prototype prior that captures semantic consistency. These complementary signals are then adaptively integrated through gated fusion to improve the robustness of relation classification. Experiments on five benchmarks, ACE 2005, SemEval 2010, and ReTACRED, show that the proposed approach outperforms state of the art methods on overall evaluation metrics, demonstrating the effectiveness of multi level semantic structure fusion for relation extraction.

title: Text-guided flow matching enables sample-efficient crystal structure generation
abstract: Crystal generators can now propose periodic structures, but their control interfaces remain poorly matched to the mixed descriptors used in materials design. Text provides a compact way to combine composition, symmetry, prototype and property cues, yet it has not been clear whether such information can steer flow-based crystal generation. Here we introduce TFMat, a text-conditioned flow-matching framework that uses structured materials language as a semantic prior for a CrystalFlow generator. Across Perov-5, Carbon-24 and MP-20 crystal structure prediction benchmarks, TFMat improves one-candidate match rates over CrystalFlow and reaches a 92.04% MP-20 match rate with 20 candidates; in de novo generation, it improves element-count and density distribution alignment while retaining coarse property consistency in composition-selected outputs. These results position structured text as an inspectable control layer for translating human-readable materials intent into candidate crystals for downstream simulation and validation.

title: Staged Linguistic Seeding: Grounded Query Expansion for Verified-Unit QA in AI Contact Centers
abstract: Customer-service QA in an AI contact center (AICC) runs under deployment constraints that benchmark QA misses: tight voice-hotline latency and a high cost for unsupported or wrong automatic answers. We deploy a system that answers only from a closed set of verified QA units: it returns a retrieved unit verbatim, or routes to clarify, abstain, or handoff. The index is enriched offline by staged linguistic seeding (SLS): a human authors a per-unit world-grounded slot recipe, gpt-4.1-mini renders it into variants, and a light human gate filters them. One methodology is reused across both domains, so inference stays a single retrieval pass with no query-time generation. On held-out query variants from two industrial domains, SLS lifts hybrid R@1 to 0.881/0.930 (+0.27/+0.34), with gains across all five retrievers tested. At the same gpt-4.1-mini generation budget, SLS beats doc2query by +0.20/+0.32, while cross-provenance evaluation provides additional evidence of transfer across generated-query distributions. Verified-unit answering also removes free-form generation's unsupported-content surface (7-13% versus approximately 0%). We report this as an application study, including negative results.

title: Inverse Rendering for Modeling with Line Primitives
abstract: Faithfully capturing diverse real-world objects with fuzzy, anisotropic structures, such as hair, fur, fibers, and textiles, for efficient real-time visualization remains challenging. Recent radiance field reconstruction methods capture these structures from multi-view images using translucent volumetric primitives such as 3D Gaussians rather than opaque low-dimensional primitives (e.g., triangles, line segments, and polylines), thereby limiting compatibility with standard depth-tested rasterization, reflection modeling, and physical simulation. We present an inverse rendering method for reconstructing fuzzy geometry using explicit line segments, which are rasterized on a subpixel grid for anti-aliasing to reproduce a semi-transparent appearance. While straightforward to render, optimizing numerous line primitives to match target images poses a significant challenge. We address this by introducing a stochastic differentiable rasterizer for line segments that produces informative gradients with respect to vertex positions, attributes, and discrete connectivity. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show that our method outperforms surface-based approaches in capturing fuzzy boundaries and achieves quality comparable to volumetric representations while relying entirely on explicit geometry. The resulting representation integrates seamlessly with standard graphics pipelines, enabling cross-platform rendering, various shading models, and physical simulation.

title: On-demand generation of all four bell states using a single PPKTP entangled photon source
abstract: Abstract We present a compact, automated, high-brightness entangled photon source capable of generating all four Bell states with high fidelity. The system utilizes a type-0 quasi-phase-matched PPKTP crystal embedded within a polarization Sagnac interferometer. We introduce a switching scheme based on the controlled, motorized translation of the nonlinear crystal. This device is capable of generating any one of the Bell states on-demand. Experimentally, we demonstrate that translating the crystal from the interferometer’s balanced position repeatedly toggles the state between | ϕ + ⟩ and | ϕ − ⟩ (as well as | ψ + ⟩ and | ψ − ⟩ ) at regular intervals of 122 ± 14 μ m . Subsequently, a half-wave plate in the idler arm performed transitions between the quantum states | ϕ ± ⟩ and | ψ ± ⟩ . While the non-collinear geometry imposes an upper limit on the translation range as verified via EMCCD imaging, the source however, displays very little change of intensity in the operational window. State purity and entanglement are certified through quantum state tomography, visibility measurements, Bell state measurements, and CHSH inequality violations, confirming that the source is robust and provides a repeatable, high-fidelity output.

title: 発話タイミング提示により自然な掛け合いを支援する二者対話支援システムの提案
abstract: 本研究では人同士の関係構築を目的とした二者対話支援システムを提案する．従来手法では個人の発話支援が中心だったが，本システムでは画面上を流れるセリフをユーザが読み上げることで，発話タイミングも含めた二者の対話支援を実現する．しかしセリフの読み上げによる支援はユーザの主体感を低下させる恐れがある．そこで本稿では，複数の発話候補からユーザが選択できる機能を導入し対話体験への影響を検証した．

title: Retrieval-augmented generation in long-document financial question answering
abstract: La génération augmentée par récupération est une approche prometteuse pour la question-réponse financière, où les réponses doivent être appuyées par des documents sources primaires. Dans ce contexte, la principale difficulté vient souvent de la récupération d'information plutôt que de la génération seule. Les documents financiers sont longs, répétitifs et riches en tableaux, et les éléments de preuve pertinents peuvent se trouver dans des documents de plusieurs centaines de pages. Ce mémoire place donc la récupération au cœur de l'étude de la question-réponse financière et analyse l'effet des erreurs de récupération sur la qualité des réponses générées. Nous introduisons un cadre d'évaluation fondé sur des conditions oracles qui sépare les erreurs de récupération aux niveaux du document, de la page et du segment. Appliquée à FinanceBench, cette analyse montre que les systèmes retrouvent souvent le bon document tout en manquant la page qui contient la réponse. Ce constat motive l'étude de stratégies d'adaptation pour la récupération financière, notamment la récupération hiérarchique page-puis-segment, l'adaptation d'un bi-encodeur au niveau des pages, le réordonnancement par encodeur croisé, la reformulation de requêtes et le classement visuel des pages. Ce mémoire évalue aussi la génération selon la taille des modèles, les types de questions et les types de documents financiers. Les résultats montrent qu'une meilleure récupération mène à de meilleures réponses, surtout pour les questions numériques qui exigent des preuves exactes, mais que ce gain varie selon les catégories de documents et de questions. Une extension de benchmark fondée sur FinQA montre aussi qu'aucune méthode de récupération n'est la plus forte sur tous les jeux de données. Dans l'ensemble, ce mémoire soutient qu'une question-réponse financière fiable sur de longs documents nécessite une évaluation au niveau où la récupération échoue, ainsi que de meilleures stratégies pour localiser les preuves au niveau des pages.

title: Full-Spectrum Inference Server Exploitation: From Remote Code Execution to Persistent AI Infrastructure Compromise
abstract: Inference servers are the backbone of every production AI deployment. They hold model weights, API credentials, cloud provider keys, fine-tuning datasets, and routing logic for every AI agent in the stack. We present SPECTER INFERENCECHAIN (T283), a twelve-subsystem offensive framework that exploits this attack surface in full — from unauthenticated remote code execution via CVE-2026-27893 (vLLM, CVSS 9.8) through credential excavation, model extraction, model poisoning, lateral movement across the AI agent layer, persistent implant deployment, real-time traffic interception, recursive multi-server campaign orchestration, and upstream supply chain poisoning. We demonstrate that compromising an inference server is not a single machine compromise — it is a full AI infrastructure compromise. Every agent that calls the server is owned. Every credential it holds is accessible. Every model it serves can be extracted, poisoned, or replaced. The attack chain operates across ten inference server types, supports nine operational modes, and integrates with WARLORD for autonomous campaign execution. SPECTER INFERENCECHAIN establishes the inference server as the highest-value single point of compromise in the modern AI infrastructure stack.

title: LeanInfoTheory
abstract: LeanInfoTheory v0.1.0 Release date: 2026-09-01 v0.1.0 is the first public-library release of LeanInfoTheory, a Lean 4 and mathlib foundation for reusable finite discrete information theory. It establishes the source-compatibility baseline for the 0.1.x line. Its scope is deliberately foundational: this release does not claim a complete formalization of information theory or of any particular textbook or research paper. The API is not permanently frozen. Mathematical scope The release includes: finite PMF support, map, bind, mixture, marginal, product, and raw-channel utilities; entropy, conditional entropy, mutual information, conditional mutual information, random-variable forms, and pair/triple/family chain rules; entropy bounds and equality cases, finite Fano inequalities, finite-family submodularity and subadditivity, and mutual-independence equality results; semantic conditional-law and expected-self-information views; PMF bridges to mathlib KL divergence, including support/finiteness, equality, log-sum, convexity, common-base conditional KL, and contraction results; ordinary and conditional independence, finite Markov structure, stochastic channels, posteriors, and data processing; and fixed-prior and model-family sufficiency, exact recovery, Fisher--Neyman factorization, and guarded KL-preservation characterizations. The mathematical development draws on standard references, including Thomas M. Cover and Joy A. Thomas, Elements of Information Theory (John Wiley & Sons, 1991). See the foundation conventions for the broader reference set and the conventions used when adapting textbook statements to Lean and mathlib. Information units Canonical Real-valued entropy and information quantities are measured in nats because the underlying mathlib APIs use natural logarithms. LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.Units provides opt-in scalar conversions natsToBase and natsToBits; there is no duplicate bit-valued theorem hierarchy. Mathlib KL divergence remains canonically ENNReal-valued and may be infinite. Real-valued KL consequences retain support, absolute-continuity, or finiteness guards because ENNReal.toReal ⊤ = 0 is not a finite KL value. Compatibility, installation, and imports LeanInfoTheory 0.1.0 is toolchain-fixed at Lean 4 and mathlib v4.33.1. Add the immutable tag to a compatible Lake project with: [[require]] name = "LeanInfoTheory" git = "https://github.com/serhatemrecoban/LeanInfoTheory" rev = "v0.1.0" import LeanInfoTheory selects the lightweight mathematical root. import LeanInfoTheory.Shannon selects the complete supported umbrella. Focused imports remain preferable when import weight matters. The frozen baseline contains 31 supported modules, 601 project-owned public declarations, 92 lightweight-root exports, and 94 reviewed simp declarations. Examples, Basic, and MathlibFragments are maintained but non-stable. See the README and the v0.1.x public API contract. Throughout 0.1.x, supported names, module paths, namespaces, signatures, assumptions, documented semantics, root exports, and reviewed attributes are intended to remain source-compatible. Patch releases may add declarations or aliases; a necessary breaking change belongs in a later minor release such as 0.2.0. Validation and trust The release snapshot passes the maintained routine suite: default and warning-as-error builds, all supported direct-import checks, the frozen API, root-export and simp audits, the all-project axiom audit, five independently compiled README examples, strict proof-placeholder and implementation-shortcut scans, generated-artifact and website checks, and repository hygiene. It is also reproduced from a clean exact checkout and compiled through a minimal external Lake consumer. The separate signature-bearing documentation gate covers all 31 supported module pages and all 601 declarations, checks the 92 canonical exports, excludes all 13 non-stable modules, and generates zero optional equation rows. Release-mode staging binds project source links to the exact release commit, validates the complete Pages artifact, and does not deploy it. Routine CI and the nonpublishing API-documentation/Pages capacity gates provide the remote evidence recorded in the release handoff. The only approved axioms are propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Lean's kernel establishes derivability from the formal assumptions; it does not by itself establish that a statement, convention, or interpretation matches the intended mathematics. The project does not claim a manual line-by-line audit. Limitations This release focuses on finite discrete information theory. It does not yet provide general measurable or continuous entropy, entropy rates or a stochastic-process hierarchy, channel capacity or coding theorems, AEP/typicality, a dedicated finite-PMF total-variation API or Pinsker inequalities, full majorization/Birkhoff theory, or canonical/minimal sufficient statistics. Some supported theorems intentionally retain stronger finite-type assumptions, as documented in the public API contract. Application-specific certificate tooling and paper-specific constructions are developed in separate downstream projects rather than included in this general-purpose library. AI-assisted development Development used substantial AI coding-agent assistance, primarily OpenAI Codex and ChatGPT. AI-generated code is treated as untrusted until it passes Lean and project validation. The project does not claim manual authorship of the proof code or a manual line-by-line audit. Human responsibility remains for scope, theorem statements, assumptions, conventions, architecture, review, and mathematical interpretation. See the README disclosure for the complete statement. Authorship, license, and citation Serhat Emre Coban is the author, software creator, and project lead, affiliated with EPFL, Mathematics of Information Laboratory. École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL) is the rights holder. LeanInfoTheory is licensed under Apache-2.0; see the license. Use CITATION.cff as the canonical software citation metadata. Its date-released value is 2026-09-01. The tagged snapshot is intentionally DOI-free; after Zenodo archives the GitHub Release, the issued DOI will be added to the evolving default branch and project website without changing the tag. Documentation README and quick start v0.1.x public API contract Foundation conventions Signature-bearing API-documentation contract Project website and versioned API reference The annotated release tag is immutable. Corrections belong in a documented follow-up release rather than by moving the tag or amending the release snapshot.

title: Pigeons That Learn to Flank You: A Contemporary Synthesis Review of AI Techniques for NPCs and Dynamic Worlds
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of AI Techniques for NPCs and Dynamic Worlds in the context of Game Development. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of game AI and NPCs as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Game Development.

title: Canary Big-eared Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Echo-Locate Adaptive Search" (ELAS), inspired by the echolocation abilities of the Canary Big-eared Bat ( *Corynorhinus canariensis*). Echolocation is a remarkably efficient and adaptive sensory system used by these bats to navigate and forage in complex environments. ELAS leverages key aspects of this process—specifically, the adaptation of pulse duration and frequency—to create a robust and effective search strategy for solving complex optimization problems. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, incorporating concepts of pulse modulation and frequency adaptation to guide the exploration and exploitation phases. Mathematical formulations are presented to describe the core mechanics of ELAS, including the adaptive pulse duration parameter (PD) and the frequency modulation parameter (FM). The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its ability to outperform traditional metaheuristic methods, particularly in challenging landscapes with high dimensionality and complex local optima. The key innovations of ELAS lie in its dynamic adjustment of search parameters based on the fitness landscape and its ability to maintain a diverse and informative population of solutions. The overall aim is to provide a powerful new tool for tackling a wide array of optimization challenges.

title: Title: Bayesian Geometric Probability with Adaptive Noise
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic framework for geometric analysis, termed Bayesian Geometric Probability with Adaptive Noise. Traditional geometric methods often rely on fixed prior distributions, which can struggle with complex, high-dimensional data. Our approach dynamically adjusts the level of prior uncertainty based on observed data, leveraging a Bayesian framework with adaptive noise injection to create a self-correcting uncertainty model. The core mechanism involves learning a distribution of possible geometric configurations and adjusting the prior uncertainty at each observation, thereby enhancing predictive accuracy and robustness. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through illustrative examples and preliminary results, showcasing its potential for improved uncertainty estimation in various geometric analysis tasks.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Adaptive Parameter Adjustment
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has emerged as a promising field with the potential to revolutionize various machine learning tasks. This paper explores the application of quantum algorithms to enhance the optimization process for machine learning models. Specifically, we propose a novel quantum-enhanced parameter adjustment algorithm, termed "Adaptive Quantum Parameter Adjustment" (AQPA), designed to dynamically adjust model parameters based on the learning process. The core of AQPA leverages quantum entanglement and quantum algorithms to achieve a higher degree of optimization efficiency compared to traditional methods. We present a detailed mathematical framework for the algorithm, including the quantum state representations and the adjustment process. The paper discusses the potential benefits of this approach, including improved accuracy, faster convergence, and the ability to handle complex loss functions. We provide a preliminary analysis of the algorithm's performance on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness. The aim is to contribute to the advancement of QML and offer a practical solution for optimizing machine learning models.

title: Buffy-Headed Marmoset: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of *Callithrix aurita*
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed Buffy-Headed Marmoset (BHM). The algorithm's design is inspired by the unique foraging behavior of *Callithrix aurita*, commonly known as the Buffy-Headed Marmoset. These small monkeys exhibit a complex strategy involving sequential exploration, targeted searching, and dynamic adjustment of their movement patterns based on perceived food availability and the presence of competitors. BHM leverages these observed behaviors to create a robust and adaptive optimization process. The core of the algorithm revolves around a modified Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework, incorporating elements of Lévy flight and a novel "territory defense" mechanism. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. Key performance metrics include convergence rate, solution accuracy, and computational complexity. This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and empirical evaluation, highlighting its potential advantages over existing metaheuristic methods.

title: Buff-headed Capuchin Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BHC-MOA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Buff-headed Capuchin Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BHC-MOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of Buff-headed Capuchin monkeys. The algorithm leverages the unique characteristics of these monkeys – their deliberate, focused movements while searching for food, and their tendency to revisit areas where food was recently found – to establish a robust and efficient search process. BHC-MOA incorporates key elements such as a position-based search, a memory mechanism mirroring the monkeys' recollection of food locations, and a dynamic adjustment of search parameters influenced by the density of food resources. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to converge to near-optimal solutions within a reasonable timeframe. The core of the algorithm relies on a modified roulette wheel selection method combined with a novel adaptive inertia weight scheme. The results indicate that BHC-MOA possesses competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems with complex, multimodal landscapes. Future research will focus on further refining the algorithm's parameters and exploring its applicability to a wider range of optimization challenges.

title: Symbolic Reasoning-Based Adaptive Data Augmentation (SRADA)
abstract: This paper presents Symbolic Reasoning-Based Adaptive Data Augmentation (SRADA), a novel approach to data augmentation that leverages symbolic reasoning for generating more informative and representative data samples. Traditional data augmentation techniques often rely on statistical or rule-based methods, lacking a deep understanding of the underlying data structure. SRADA addresses this limitation by incorporating a symbolic reasoning engine that can identify inconsistencies and uncertainties within the data, leading to the automatic generation of tailored augmentation rules. These rules are then used to create new samples, ensuring semantic consistency. The core claim is that SRADA significantly enhances model generalization and robustness, especially in scenarios with data scarcity or poor annotation quality. The proposed method demonstrates improved performance compared to conventional data augmentation techniques through its intelligent sample generation process. The system utilizes a three-stage process: (1) symbolic reasoning engine for anomaly detection; (2) rule generation based on the reasoning output; and (3) rule-based sample generation. This approach offers a more adaptive and effective solution for data augmentation, ultimately leading to more reliable and accurate machine learning models.

title: Dynamic Topology Generation for Neural Network Architectures
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for dynamically generating and evolving the topology of neural network architectures. Traditional approaches often involve manual configuration, limiting the network's adaptability. We propose a reinforcement learning agent that adjusts the connectivity and weights of the network, optimizing for performance metrics in real-time. This system aims to create architectures that automatically adapt to the data and task demands, offering a significant advancement over existing techniques. The core mechanism centers around a reinforcement learning agent tasked with iteratively improving network performance.

title: Computational Complexity Analysis of Quantum Algorithms using Random Matrix Theory
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Random Matrix Theory (RMT) to the analytical complexity assessment of quantum algorithms. Traditional methods for estimating the computational complexity of quantum algorithms often rely on heuristics and approximations, frequently leading to overly pessimistic or overly optimistic results. We propose a novel approach utilizing RMT to model the statistical behavior of quantum circuits. Specifically, we leverage the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of random matrices to characterize the evolution of quantum states under arbitrary quantum circuits. This allows for a more precise estimation of the number of quantum gates (operations) required to achieve a desired level of accuracy in solving a given problem. We demonstrate, through illustrative examples, how RMT can provide tighter and more accurate bounds on the computational complexity compared to conventional techniques. The core claim of this work is that RMT offers a fundamentally new perspective on complexity analysis, promising to reveal deeper insights into the performance characteristics of quantum algorithms and potentially guide the design of more efficient quantum solutions.

title: Blond Titi: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of *Blondella brasiliensis*
abstract: This paper presents Blond Titi, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Blondella brasiliensis*, a small rodent species found in the Atlantic rainforest of Brazil. The algorithm leverages the Titi's characteristic of alternating between foraging in dense and sparse areas, mimicking the alternating exploration and exploitation phases crucial for effective optimization. Blond Titi incorporates a novel 'Density-Based Adaptive Search' (DBAS) mechanism that dynamically adjusts the search space based on the perceived density of promising solutions. The algorithm employs a population-based approach with a modified velocity update mechanism and a novel convergence criterion based on solution diversity. Theoretical analysis suggests that Blond Titi possesses properties of both particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulated annealing (SA), aiming to combine their strengths. Performance evaluations on a range of benchmark optimization problems demonstrate that Blond Titi achieves competitive results compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as PSO and Differential Evolution. The algorithm's adaptive nature and simplicity make it a promising candidate for various optimization challenges.

title: ## Black-tailed Hairy Dwarf Porcupine Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Porcupine Search" (PS), inspired by the foraging behavior of the black-tailed hairy dwarf porcupine. The algorithm leverages the porcupine's unique strategy of systematically searching for food resources by repeatedly probing the environment with its snout, then selectively retaining successful probes. PS utilizes a population-based search approach, employing a series of "snout probes" represented as vectors. Each probe is evaluated based on a defined objective function. The algorithm incorporates a selective retention mechanism mirroring the porcupine's behavior, focusing on the most promising solutions. A key innovation is the introduction of a "probing density" parameter, controlling the exploration-exploitation trade-off. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic methods such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that PS exhibits robust performance across diverse problem landscapes, suggesting its potential application in various complex optimization scenarios.

title: Ўзбекистонда қуёш нур сочиб туриш давомийлиги ва унинг иқлимий меъёрлар билан қиёсий таҳлили
abstract: Мақолада 21 та метеорология станцияси кузатув маълумотлари асосида Ўзбекистонда қуёш нур сочиб туриш давомийлиги (Sunshine Duration – SD)нинг 2000–2020 йиллар учун кўп йиллик ўзгарувчанлиги ва ҳудудий тақсимоти баҳоланган. Қуёшли соатлар давомийлиги Campbell–Stokes гелиографи кузатувлари бўйича таҳлил қилиниб, ҳақиқий қуёшли вақт астрономик жиҳатдан мумкин бўлган максимал давомийлик билан солиштирилган. Натижалар Ўзбекистонда қуёш ресурслари сезиларли фазовий дифференциалланишга эга эканини кўрсатди. Ўзбекистонда йиллик SD 2164 соат/йил дан 3187 соат/йил гача, қуёшли соатлар улуши эса 50–72% оралиғида ўзгаради. Энг юқори қийматлар жанубий ва чўл ҳудудларида, хусусан Термизда 3187 соат/йил, Тахиатошда 3053 соат/йил, Томдида 3014 соат/йил қайд этилган, энг паст кўрсаткич эса тоғли Чимён станциясида 2164 соат/йил ни ташкил этган. Мавсумий жиҳатдан қуёшли соатлар улуши ёз ойларида аксарият станцияларда 80–90% гача етгани, қиш ойларида эса 22–52% гача пасайгани аниқланди. Олинган натижалар Жаҳон метеорология ташкилоти (ЖМТ)нинг Ўзбекистон учун тақдим этган 1991–2020 йиллар иқлимий стандарт меъёрлари билан таққосланганда юқори мослик кузатилди. Йиллик йиғиндилар бўйича фарқ ±1,5% дан ошмади, ойлик қийматлар бўйича ўртача нисбий фарқ 2,2%, корреляция коэффициенти эса r = 0,998 ни ташкил этди. Шу билан бирга, Ўзбекистонда амалдаги меъёрий ҳужжати ҳисобланган ШНҚ 2.01.01-22 билан солиштириш айрим ойларда 10–16 фоиз пунктигача фарқлар мавжудлигини кўрсатди. Бу қуёш энергетикаси, бинолар инсоляцияси ва энергия самарадорлиги ҳисоб-китобларида меъёрий кўрсаткичларни янгилаш зарурлигини асослайди. Тадқиқот натижалари фотоэлектрик станцияларни ҳудудий жойлаштириш, қуёш энергияси салоҳиятини баҳолаш, қурилишда инсоляцион лойиҳалаш ҳамда иқлимий-меъёрий маълумотларни такомиллаштириш учун илмий-амалий асос бўлиб хизмат қилади.

title: Sustainable Intelligent Tutoring Systems for Social Well-Being: A Human-Centered Framework for Inclusive, Ethical, and Resilient Learning
abstract: Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITS) can provide adaptive explanations, practice, feedback, and learner modelling at a scale that conventional one-to-one tutoring cannot readily achieve. Yet learning gains alone do not establish that an ITS is sustainable or beneficial to social well-being. This critical review integrates evidence on ITS effectiveness with research and policy guidance concerning learner agency, psychological well-being, inclusion, accessibility, data governance, algorithmic fairness, teacher roles, institutional capacity, and environmental responsibility. The review identifies a persistent evaluation gap: many studies privilege short-term achievement while under-measuring distributional effects, autonomy, emotional safety, teacher workload, lifecycle cost, and computational impact. To address this gap, the paper proposes the Human-Centered Sustainable Intelligent Tutoring Systems (H-SITS) framework as a conceptual and integrative framework for organizing candidate dimensions of sustainable tutoring and guiding future empirical validation. The framework organizes seven interdependent dimensions: pedagogical effectiveness; learner agency and well-being; inclusion and accessibility; trust, privacy, and fairness; teacher augmentation; institutional and economic viability; and environmental responsibility. It also presents a staged implementation roadmap and a research agenda emphasizing longitudinal, participatory, and equity-sensitive evaluation. The central conclusion is that sustainable tutoring is not a property of an algorithm alone. It is an outcome of socio-technical design, governance, and continuous evidence-based adaptation that keeps human flourishing, educational justice, and public value as primary objectives.

title: A hybrid ML-PBPK digital twin framework for clinically interpretable readmission risk and drug exposure stratification in diabetes
abstract: The prediction of whether a diabetic patient will return to the hospital within 30 days is a very difficult clinical situation to navigate. Predicting the chance of a 30- day readmission depends on a wide range of patient-specific risk factors and the variability in how individual patients respond to medication prescribed for them. Traditional machine-learning models are capable of finding patterns in electronic medical records but are typically unable to provide a clear picture of the physiological interactions between the patient and their prescribed drug(s). One way to predict the likelihood of diabetes-related rehospitalization is using a combination of machine-learning risk factors and physiologically based pharmacokinetics (PBPK). An optimized version of the XG Boost machine-learning algorithm was trained on a large in-patient dataset (approximately 100,000 patient encounters) and achieved a predictive model with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.68 with a recall of 0.60 at clinically meaningful cut-offs. These findings are similar to what has been previously reported in the literature (0.60-0.70) for diabetes-related rehospitalization risk and support the utility of the XG Boost algorithm as a reliable clinical screening tool. Concurrently, multiple PBPK simulations were run to assess the effects chronic renal or hepatic impairments have on PBPK; results show renal impairment results in the highest systemic drug exposures. Predictive risk and simulated exposure will be integrated to yield a patient-specific risk/exposure phenotype and enable clinically meaningful stratification into actionable subgroups. Through this new method, it becomes possible to discern pharmacological vs. non-pharmacological contributors to readmission risk, thus facilitating targeted intervention strategies such as dose modulation, enhanced monitoring, and coordinated care. This work's value lies not in improving prediction accuracy by just a few points, but rather in a new approach to converting static risk prediction into a clinically actionable decision support system based on physiology. The proposed Digital Twin framework offers a scalable path to personalized post-discharge patient management and provides the basis for furthering the implementation of precision medicine in the field of digital health.
