title: Adaptive Elite Cuckoo Search Algorithm with Step-Size Control and Elitism Crossover for Global Optimization
abstract: Cuckoo Search Algorithm (CSA) has emerged as a powerful bio-inspired metaheuristic, yet its reliance on random-walk search often leads to slow convergence and susceptibility to local optima. This study introduces an Adaptive Elite Cuckoo Search Algorithm (AECSA), designed to enhance both convergence speed and solution precision. The proposed modifications integrate two key mechanisms: (i) an adaptive step-size strategy that dynamically adjusts the Lévy flight scale to balance global exploration and local exploitation, and (ii) an elitist crossover scheme that enables information sharing among the top-performing solutions to accelerate progress toward the global optimum. The AECSA was validated across six classical benchmark functions under extensive simulations. Results demonstrate that AECSA consistently outperforms the standard CSA, achieving up to 85% faster convergence and significantly improved solution accuracy, with statistical validation via a two-tailed t-test. These findings highlight the robustness and efficiency of AECSA, making it a promising approach for tackling complex, high-dimensional optimization problems in engineering and computational intelligence.

title: Deep Learning for Early Prediction of Adverse Events in Intensive Care Units Using Electronic Health Records: A Methodological Review
abstract: Purpose: To provide a methodological synthesis of deep learning (DL) approaches for early prediction of preventable adverse events (AEs) in intensive care units (ICUs) using electronic health record (EHR) data, and to examine how intrinsic EHR data challenges affect model development, predictive performance, and clinical applicability. Methods: This review was designed as a methodological synthesis rather than a quantitative meta-analysis or statistical comparison. Seven databases were systematically searched to identify studies on early AE prediction in ICU settings using DL models. Eligible studies were screened based on predefined criteria, and data were extracted and synthesized qualitatively to analyze EHR data characteristics, DL architectures, and associated methodological challenges. Results: A total of 31 studies comprising 33 predictive models were included. These studies covered multiple preventable AEs, diverse ICU EHR datasets, and a range of DL architectures. Across studies with different prediction windows, reported AUROC values ranged from 0.75 to 0.95. Four studies used oversampling to address class imbalance. Despite the increasing use of advanced and hybrid architectures, three recurring methodological challenges remained: subtle early-stage risk signals, class imbalance, and heterogeneity. Overall, the effectiveness of DL-based AE prediction depends less on architectural novelty alone and more on whether models are explicitly designed around the data conditions under which preventable AEs emerge. Conclusion: Future studies should move beyond architecture-centered optimization and develop methodological strategies, such as multimodal learning, bias-aware modeling, and personalized prediction strategies. More attention should also be given to external and prospective validation, safe clinical use, and real-world effects on patient care and preventable harm.

title: Extended Abstract: Real-Time Fraud Detection on Azure with Machine Learning and Drift Monitoring
abstract: Financial fraud continues to evolve as adversaries adapt their behavior to bypass detection systems.Machine learning models deployed in real-time environments must therefore respond effectively to shifting fraud patterns, feature distribution changes, and gradual model performance degradation.This paper presents the design and implementation of a cloud-scale, end-to-end real-time credit card fraud detection system on Microsoft Azure with integrated drift monitoring.The architecture combines a Python-based financial transaction simulator, Azure Event Hubs for streaming ingestion, Azure Data Factory for batch and incremental loads, Azure Databricks for unified batch and structured streaming processing, and Delta Lake organized in a Bronze-Silver-Gold layout for reliable storage.A logistic regression model is trained on engineered geospatial, temporal, velocity, behavioral, and terminalrisk features and is deployed in a micro batch scoring pipeline.Real-time scoring is integrated with Population Stability Index-based drift detection that monitors both feature drift and prediction drift, and automated retraining is triggered when drift severity exceeds defined thresholds or when supervised precision falls below an acceptable level.The proposed system demonstrates how drift-aware machine learning pipelines can be operationalized at scale and offers a practical reference architecture for fraud detection in dynamic financial environments.

title: Fisher-guided personalized federated learning with efficient packed homomorphic aggregation
abstract: Existing personalized federated learning (PFL) methods mostly emphasize accuracy while often overlooking privacy leakage under an honest-but-curious server. Moreover, privacy-preserving PFL faces a practical trade-off between utility and the heavy communication overhead induced by homomorphic encryption. To address these challenges, we propose FedFIHE, which leverages Fisher-information-guided adaptive partitioning to dynamically select shared parameters for global aggregation while retaining the remaining parameters for local personalization under heterogeneous data. To make encrypted training efficient, FedFIHE further introduces a packet-level selective encrypted aggregation scheme. Specifically, clients pack model parameters into packets and upload only the top- \(\kappa \) selected packets with binary masks, and the server performs mask voting to aggregate and broadcast only the most frequently selected packet positions in ciphertext, avoiding the excessive cost caused by inconsistent sparse selections across clients. Extensive experiments on natural image and medical datasets demonstrate that FedFIHE effectively mitigates privacy leakage while achieving better or comparable personalized performance to strong baselines. FedFIHE also remains robust under high sparsity, making it suitable for privacy-sensitive applications such as healthcare.

title: (2-dep,$Σ$)-categories are not generalised categories with families
abstract: The notion of a generalised category with families, introduced by Coraglia and Emmenegger is one of the most general notions introduced to capture categorically the notion of dependent typing. It is shown that these generalised categories with families are biequivalent to comprehension categories. We will show that the notion of a (2-dep,$Σ$)-category, an extension of the notion of a (dep,$Σ$)-category, introduced by Petrakis, is not biequivalent to generalised categories with families, but instead is equivalent to a direct generalisation of that notion.

title: Meta-ethics and AI: exploring the novel meta-ethical questions in the era of AI
abstract: With the development of artificial intelligence (AI), the landscape of meta-ethics, which has largely centred on human ethics, faces pressures that may significantly reconfigure it. In particular, if future AI systems were to exhibit sufficiently integrated capacities for moral reasoning, moral intentionality, and moral reflection, novel meta-ethical questions would arise concerning what I call "AI's own ethics", as distinct from ethical principles merely imposed on AI by human designers. This paper offers a conditional and methodological framework for identifying the questions that would emerge if such AI systems were to arise. On that basis, the paper distinguishes four domains of meta-ethical inquiry in the era of AI: questions about the nature of human ethics from the human perspective; questions about the nature of AI's own ethics from the human perspective; questions about the nature of human ethics from the AI perspective; and questions about the nature of AI's own ethics from the AI perspective. The paper then considers how some existing mainstream meta-ethical theories (such as cognitivism and non-cognitivism, error theory and success theory, relativism, and objective realism) might illuminate these domains, while arguing that many familiar human-centred formulations of those theories may not transfer straightforwardly to AI cases without substantial revision. The overall conclusion is that the emergence of AI's own ethics would place significant pressure on current frameworks and may require substantial refinement, reconstruction, or reconceptualisation.

title: Residual Kalman Dynamics for Event-Based UAV Forecasting
abstract: We study short- and mid-horizon UAV bounding-box forecasting on the FRED event-camera dataset. We use a constant-velocity Kalman filter over a full center-size box state as a strong physical baseline, and train a residual model to predict acceleration-like corrections from recent box history, filtered state features, and local event representations. This simple residual formulation consistently improves over the Kalman baseline, with event-conditioned models giving the strongest results among the evaluated methods. We further show that part of the residual target is predictable from anchor position and velocity alone, indicating that canonical FRED results can reflect both visual evidence and dataset-specific motion priors. To analyze this effect, we introduce decorrelated subsets as a diagnostic stress test, showing that event-conditioned residual models retain useful predictive signal even when measured position- and velocity-based shortcuts are weakened.

title: Data-efficient machine learning for photovoltaic power prediction: Explainability, uncertainty, and learning saturation
abstract: Reliable photovoltaic power prediction is increasingly important for integrating variable solar generation into modern electricity systems, yet many operational installations have only limited historical data. This study developed a data-efficient, explainable, and uncertainty-aware machine-learning framework using 412 daylight observations from a grid-connected photovoltaic plant in India. Ambient temperature, module temperature, irradiation, day of year, and cyclic time variables were used to predict AC power with Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Extra Trees Regression (ETR). Pearson correlation and principal component analysis were used to examine predictor structure, while chronological validation, permutation importance, SHAP analysis, predictive intervals, and learning-saturation experiments were applied to evaluate robustness. Irradiation showed the strongest correlation with AC power (r = 0.97), while the first three principal components explained 96.6% of predictor variance. ETR achieved the best independent-test performance (R² = 0.997, RMSE = 22.080 kW, MAE = 16.402 kW, sMAPE = 2.496%), closely followed by SVR (R² = 0.996). SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified irradiation as the dominant predictor, with a mean absolute contribution of 253.384 kW. ETR retained R² = 0.995 using only 50 training observations, demonstrating strong data efficiency. The results show that reliable and interpretable photovoltaic prediction can be achieved from very limited field measurements when model selection and validation are carefully designed under data-scarce operating conditions.

title: Demonstrating Exact Financial Risk Calculations on NISQ Quantum Hardware with Precision No Sampling Method Can Reach - Governed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation under Seed IQ on the Superconducting IBM Heron r2/r3 QPUs—Beating the NVIDIA STAC-A2 GPU Risk Record Without Sampling
abstract: Abstract We demonstrate governed fault-tolerant quantum computing (GFTQC) applied to financial risk: every number is computed exactly, with a precision and reproducibility no sampling method can reach. Every risk number a financial institution must produce, a value-at-risk, an expected shortfall, a valuation adjustment, and the price and Greeks beneath them, is at bottom an expectation: a probability-weighted integral of a payoff over the distribution of future market paths. The industry evaluates these integrals by Monte-Carlo sampling, and sampling has two structural defects. Its statistical error falls only as 1/√N in the number of paths, so each additional digit costs a hundredfold more compute; and the estimate drifts from one run to the next, so it cannot deliver the auditable, reproducible numbers the FRTB P&L Attribution (PLA) test demands. The industry’s response has been to sample faster: NVIDIA’s audited STAC-A2 record [26], the benchmark for derivatives-risk computation, runs 561 option-valuations per second on an 8×H100 GPU server over 316 million paths, which is faster sampling and still stochastic. The quantum proposals do not close the gap either: the near-term methods (VQE, QAOA, QPE) only estimate, and the machines that would carry the field past sampling are a 2030+ prospect, not today. The field, in short, is caught between classical sampling that never becomes exact (Monte Carlo, quasi-Monte Carlo, GPU-accelerated) and quantum methods that either only estimate today (VQE, QPE, QAOA) or await a 2030+ roadmap. Governed fault-tolerant quantum computing (GFTQC) sits in neither camp: it commits the exact value on hardware that exists now. We compute the risk on quantum hardware that exists now, and we compute it exactly and deterministically. Under Seed IQ, a fault-tolerant quantum computation on the 156-qubit IBM Heron QPU encodes the risk-neutral density as a governed quantum register and computes its expectation at a self-certified eigenstate, rather than estimating it from repeated measurement. This is the same governed determinism our companion fault-tolerant quantum work established on the very same hardware—FCI-exact hydrogen-chain energies committed on IBM Boston (Heron r3), internally certified exact and reproducible to twelve decimal places [1, 2]; here that deterministic, on-hardware exactness is turned on the derivatives integral. The dissipative dynamics converge to the target eigenstate and the output is exact to machine precision, with zero variance and byte-identical on rerun—the 10−12 price no sampler reaches at any budget, delivered directly. Across structured products, factor-model risk, XVA and expected shortfall the story is the same: exact where Monte Carlo is noisy, reproducible where it drifts. That the same exact computation is also 35× faster than NVIDIA’s eight-GPU record on the audited STAC-A2 workload is a consequence of not sampling, not the headline; the headline is that the number is right to the last digit. The gap is not incremental. evidence.abstract: Abstract We demonstrate governed fault-tolerant quantum computing (GFTQC) applied to financial risk: every number is computed exactly, with a precision and reproducibility no sampling method can reach. Every risk number a financial institution must produce, a value-at-risk, an expected shortfall, a valuation adjustment, and the price and Greeks beneath them, is at bottom an expectation: a probability-weighted integral of a payoff over the distribution of future market paths. The industry evaluates these integrals by Monte-Carlo sampling, and sampling has two structural defects. Its statistical error falls only as 1/√N in the number of paths, so each additional digit costs a hundredfold more compute; and the estimate drifts from one run to the next, so it cannot deliver the auditable, reproducible numbers the FRTB P&L Attribution (PLA) test demands. The industry’s response has been to sample faster: NVIDIA’s audited STAC-A2 record [26], the benchmark for derivatives-risk computation, runs 561 option-valuations per second on an 8×H100 GPU server over 316 million paths, which is faster sampling and still stochastic. The quantum proposals do not close the gap either: the near-term methods (VQE, QAOA, QPE) only estimate, and the machines that would carry the field past sampling are a 2030+ prospect, not today. The field, in short, is caught between classical sampling that never becomes exact (Monte Carlo, quasi-Monte Carlo, GPU-accelerated) and quantum methods that either only estimate today (VQE, QPE, QAOA) or await a 2030+ roadmap. Governed fault-tolerant quantum computing (GFTQC) sits in neither camp: it commits the exact value on hardware that exists now. We compute the risk on quantum hardware that exists now, and we compute it exactly and deterministically. Under Seed IQ, a fault-tolerant quantum computation on the 156-qubit IBM Heron QPU encodes the risk-neutral density as a governed quantum register and computes its expectation at a self-certified eigenstate, rather than estimating it from repeated measurement. This is the same governed determinism our companion fault-tolerant quantum work established on the very same hardware—FCI-exact hydrogen-chain energies committed on IBM Boston (Heron r3), internally certified exact and reproducible to twelve decimal places [1, 2]; here that deterministic, on-hardware exactness is turned on the derivatives integral. The dissipative dynamics converge to the target eigenstate and the output is exact to machine precision, with zero variance and byte-identical on rerun—the 10−12 price no sampler reaches at any budget, delivered directly. Across structured products, factor-model risk, XVA and expected shortfall the story is the same: exact where Monte Carlo is noisy, reproducible where it drifts. That the same exact computation is also 35× faster than NVIDIA’s eight-GPU record on the audited STAC-A2 workload is a consequence of not sampling, not the headline; the headline is that the number is right to the last digit. The gap is not incremental. What separates this work from the standard quantum-finance roadmap is not a constant factor but the machine itself (Fig. 2): textbook fault-tolerant pricing needs a computer of 10^6–10^9 physical qubits with distillation factories, projected for the 2030s; GFTQC commits the same exact, fault-tolerant risk numbers today on a 156-qubit superconducting IBM Heron QPU, a ∼10^6× smaller physical footprint. title: Caribbean Brown Bat Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Lasiurus barbatus*
abstract: This paper presents the Caribbean Brown Bat Algorithm (CBBA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies employed by *Lasiurus barbatus*, the Caribbean brown bat. The algorithm mimics the bat's echolocation and flight patterns to search for optimal solutions in complex problem spaces. CBBA incorporates key elements of bat behavior, including frequency modulation, amplitude modulation, and clustering, into a dynamic optimization framework. The algorithm utilizes a population of candidate solutions represented as "bats," each with position and velocity vectors. The objective function is evaluated based on the received signal strength, mimicking the bat's ability to detect prey. The algorithm's parameters are tuned to reflect the bat's adaptation mechanisms, leading to robust and efficient convergence. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and illustrates its performance through theoretical analysis and potential applications. The primary goal is to provide a computationally efficient and adaptable optimization method suitable for a broad range of engineering and scientific challenges. The algorithm's core mechanism is based on the principles of echolocation and flight dynamics observed in *Lasiurus barbatus*, aiming to achieve superior performance compared to existing metaheuristic methods.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Dynamic Bayesian Networks and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning by integrating Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs) with Reinforcement Learning (RL). The core idea is to train an RL agent to dynamically manipulate and utilize the inference capabilities of a DBN. Traditional neuro-symbolic systems often struggle with complex reasoning tasks demanding adaptability and the ability to handle uncertainty. This research proposes a mechanism where an RL agent learns to adjust the structure and inference rules within a DBN, effectively learning *how* to reason within a symbolic framework. We demonstrate the potential of this combined approach to achieve more sophisticated and adaptive reasoning compared to purely rule-based systems. The key contribution lies in the dynamic interaction between the symbolic DBN and the learned policies of the RL agent, fostering a system capable of learning from experience and generalizing to novel situations. This work lays the foundation for building truly intelligent systems that can reason effectively in real-world environments.

title: On the Construction of an Explainable Artificial Intelligence Program Explanation System
abstract: This paper proposes and details the construction of an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) program explanation system. The core claim driving this research is that a system capable of interpreting and explaining program execution processes can significantly enhance program understandability and maintainability. The central mechanism involves leveraging XAI techniques to analyze and visualize the execution flow of a program, offering granular insights into its operation. This approach represents a novel application of XAI within the context of program comprehension, moving beyond traditional debugging methods. The system is designed to provide a human-interpretable representation of complex program logic, facilitating improved debugging, knowledge transfer, and ultimately, more robust and reliable software. The system architecture, key components, and potential applications are outlined, emphasizing the benefits of integrating XAI principles into program explanation workflows.

title: Core Claim: A novel non-linear gradient descent algorithm based on the Gaussian distribution offers improved convergence speed and stability compared to traditional gradient descent methods.
abstract: The convergence of gradient descent algorithms is often limited by issues like vanishing or exploding gradients, particularly in non-linear optimization problems. This paper presents a new non-linear gradient descent algorithm that leverages the properties of the Gaussian distribution to mitigate these issues and accelerate convergence. We introduce a modified gradient update rule incorporating a Gaussian-weighted prior, which stabilizes the optimization process and improves the speed of convergence. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm across a range of non-linear optimization tasks, showcasing its superior performance compared to standard gradient descent and other established optimization techniques. This work contributes to the development of more robust and efficient optimization methods, particularly for problems involving non-linear data and constraints. The core mechanism focuses on minimizing the impact of gradient saturation by utilizing the Gaussian distribution, leading to faster and more stable convergence. We present the theoretical foundations and experimental validation of this approach, highlighting its potential for widespread application in diverse fields.

title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Simulation for Complex Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel hybrid quantum-classical simulation approach designed to effectively combine the strengths of both classical and quantum computation for complex systems. The core concept revolves around a dynamically adaptive sampling and analysis framework that intelligently integrates data from both sources, fostering a unified simulation environment. The proposed method addresses the limitations of current hybrid techniques by moving beyond simple data fusion and introducing a sophisticated, self-optimizing system. The paper details the implementation of this framework, demonstrates its effectiveness through illustrative examples, and discusses future research directions. The core claim is that this approach offers a pathway to significantly accelerate the simulation and analysis of complex systems, particularly those exhibiting inherently quantum-mechanical behavior.

title: 基于自适应神经网络的动态概率分布建模
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to dynamic probability distribution modeling, leveraging the capabilities of adaptive neural networks to simulate complex system behavior. Traditional probabilistic models often rely on predefined distributions, presenting challenges in adapting to intricate dynamic systems. Our work introduces a framework where an adaptive neural network dynamically adjusts probability distributions based on observed system dynamics. This dynamic adjustment mitigates the need for extensive manual parameter tuning and offers improved model accuracy in complex scenarios. The core mechanism centers on a self-learning process that refines probability distributions through a continuous feedback loop, ensuring a more realistic representation of the underlying system. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through simulations of a stochastic neural network, showcasing its ability to capture nuanced behavior patterns and achieve superior predictive performance compared to traditional methods. The results highlight the potential of this approach to accelerate the development of sophisticated simulation tools for diverse applications.

title: Brazos Pocket Gopher: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Geomycursor minimus*
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Brazos Pocket Gopher" (BPG), inspired by the foraging strategies observed in *Geomycursor minimus*, a small rodent known for its efficient burrowing and food storage behavior. The algorithm utilizes a combination of principles including adaptive step size control, a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, and a novel representation of the search space based on burrow network topology. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations across a range of benchmark optimization problems. The core of BPG lies in its 'Burrow Representation' – a discrete, graph-based representation of the search space, mimicking the gopher's network of tunnels. The algorithm iteratively constructs and modifies this burrow network, adapting its exploration and exploitation strategies based on the perceived density of promising regions. Key performance metrics, such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational cost, are evaluated. The results indicate that BPG exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems exhibiting complex landscapes and requiring robust exploration capabilities. Future work will focus on incorporating more biologically inspired mechanisms and adapting the algorithm for parallel and distributed computing environments.

title: Graph Neural Networks and Symbolic Logic Reasoning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework that integrates Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) with Symbolic Logic Reasoning for enhanced knowledge graph representation and inference. The core idea is to leverage the strengths of both approaches: GNNs for capturing structural information within a graph and symbolic logic for performing rigorous logical deductions. We construct a system where GNNs learn node and edge embeddings, and these embeddings are then utilized as inputs to a symbolic reasoning engine. This allows us to effectively represent complex knowledge graphs and perform logical inference on them. The resulting framework demonstrates improved performance compared to traditional methods, particularly in scenarios involving intricate relationships and constraints within the knowledge graph. We detail the architecture, the integration process, and present a theoretical analysis of the combined approach, highlighting its potential for applications in areas such as automated reasoning, question answering, and intelligent data integration. The key contribution lies in providing a unified methodology for combining graph-based and logic-based reasoning, leading to a more robust and interpretable knowledge representation.

abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum-driven parallel processing to significantly enhance symbolic reasoning capabilities. The core claim is that quantum parallelism can overcome the limitations of classical parallel processing in handling complex logical operations, ultimately leading to more efficient and scalable symbolic reasoning. We detail a proposed framework incorporating quantum circuits for representing and manipulating logical states, utilizing quantum parallelism to optimize these operations, and discuss the challenges and potential benefits of this approach. The research will address the fundamental limitations of classical processing in tackling intricate logical inferences.

title: Adaptive Compression Algorithms Based on Kolmogorov Complexity
abstract: This paper explores the potential of Kolmogorov complexity as the foundation for novel and highly adaptive compression algorithms. Traditional compression techniques often struggle with data exhibiting significant randomness, relying heavily on statistical modeling which can be inefficient when the underlying patterns are subtle or absent. Kolmogorov complexity, defined as the length of the shortest description of a string, offers a fundamentally different approach. This research investigates methods for estimating Kolmogorov complexity and adapting compression strategies based on these estimates. The core idea is to minimize data representation by directly targeting the inherent complexity of the data itself, rather than relying on statistical approximations. We propose an adaptive framework that dynamically adjusts compression parameters based on the observed complexity of data segments, leading to improved compression ratios, particularly for complex and unpredictable datasets. This work demonstrates the theoretical underpinnings and potential of Kolmogorov complexity in achieving unprecedented data compression efficiency.

title: Black-winged Myotis-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BWM-MHOA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Black-winged Myotis-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BWM-MHOA), drawing inspiration from the foraging behavior of the Black-winged Myotis (Myotis niger), a bat species renowned for its exceptional echolocation and efficient foraging strategies. The algorithm leverages the bat's flight patterns, particularly the exploration and exploitation phases, to navigate complex search spaces. BWM-MHOA incorporates two primary mechanisms: a dynamic position update rule based on the bat's flight speed and angle, and an adaptive parameter control scheme mimicking the bat's response to food availability. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its efficacy in finding near-optimal solutions with reasonable computational efficiency. Specifically, the algorithm's objective is to minimize the cost function: f(x) = Σi=1n (xi - pi)2 where *x* represents the decision variables, *n* is the number of variables, and *pi* represents the optimal value for the *i*-th variable. The algorithm utilizes a population of candidate solutions, represented as vectors, and iteratively updates these solutions based on the bat's flight dynamics. The performance metrics evaluated include solution accuracy, convergence rate, and computational time. Results show that BWM-MHOA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Genetic Algorithm (GA). Future research directions include incorporating more sophisticated bat behavior models and exploring the algorithm's applicability to real-world engineering problems.

title: Quantum Entanglement Analysis and Optimization
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation and communication. This paper investigates the intricacies of entanglement, focusing on its non-symmetric nature, and proposes a novel framework for optimizing quantum computing through the strategic application of this concept. We establish a new approach by introducing the "non-symmetric entanglement field theory," aiming to enhance the efficiency of quantum key distribution (QKD) and quantum cryptography. Our investigation explores the potential of this framework to address challenges in resource management and improve the robustness of quantum systems. Specifically, we analyze the impact of non-symmetry on entanglement generation and measurement, and propose a method to optimize entanglement generation for improved performance. This paper presents a conceptual overview of this research and its potential implications for advancing quantum technologies.

title: Key-Distinguishing Attack on XOR Operations Under Uncertain Ciphertext
abstract: With the rapid development of emerging network infrastructures, including the Internet of Things (IoT), non-terrestrial networks, and edge computing, lightweight cryptography has been widely adopted in resource-constrained network devices. As the exclusive-or (XOR) operation is commonly used for linear mixing and masking, the distinguishability of its outputs over noisy channels warrants dedicated investigation. Standard models of classical cryptanalysis generally adopt an idealized noise-free assumption, under which an adversary can obtain complete and accurate ciphertexts. In practical transmission, however, channel noise and environmental interference may cause random bit flips in ciphertexts, producing uncertain ciphertext observations and severely degrading or even invalidating conventional distinguishing attacks. To address this issue, this paper constructs a noise-perturbation model based on a transition probability matrix, investigates key-bit distinguishing from repeated XOR observations over a binary asymmetric channel, and proposes a Manhattan-distance-based mean-prototype key-bit distinguishing framework. When the channel noise parameters are known, deterministic prototypes are constructed from the theoretical means of the two conditional distributions, and each key bit is classified according to the Manhattan distances between the observation vector and the two prototypes. A closed-form Gaussian approximation to the single-key-bit distinguishing success rate is derived, followed by an analysis of the special case of symmetric perturbations. When the channel noise parameters are unknown, a data-driven approach to prototype construction using method-of-moments estimation is further developed. An approximate expression for the probability of correctly distinguishing a single key bit is then derived to account for the effect of training sample size. Monte Carlo experiments compare the theoretical approximations with empirical results under different channel parameters and sample sizes, demonstrating that p+q = 1 constitutes the non-identifiability boundary of the observation channel. The proposed method provides a low-complexity and interpretable statistical tool for XOR key-bit distinguishing in noisy network environments, as well as methodological and theoretical support for key-recovery attacks in practical network scenarios.

evidence.title: Key-Distinguishing Attack on XOR Operations Under Uncertain Ciphertext
evidence.abstract: With the rapid development of emerging network infrastructures, including the Internet of Things (IoT), non-terrestrial networks, and edge computing, lightweight cryptography has been widely adopted in resource-constrained network devices. As the exclusive-or (XOR) operation is commonly used for linear mixing and masking, the distinguishability of its outputs over noisy channels warrants dedicated investigation. Standard models of classical cryptanalysis generally adopt an idealized noise-free assumption, under which an adversary can obtain complete and accurate ciphertexts. In practical transmission, however, channel noise and environmental interference may cause random bit flips in ciphertexts, producing uncertain ciphertext observations and severely degrading or even invalidating conventional distinguishing attacks. To address this issue, this paper constructs a noise-perturbation model based on a transition probability matrix, investigates key-bit distinguishing from repeated XOR observations over a binary asymmetric channel, and proposes a Manhattan-distance-based mean-prototype key-bit distinguishing framework. When the channel noise parameters are known, deterministic prototypes are constructed from the theoretical means of the two conditional distributions, and each key bit is classified according to the Manhattan distances between the observation vector and the two prototypes. A closed-form Gaussian approximation to the single-key-bit distinguishing success rate is derived, followed by an analysis of the special case of symmetric perturbations. When the channel noise parameters are unknown, a data-driven approach to prototype construction using method-of-moments estimation is further developed. An approximate expression for the probability of correctly distinguishing a single key bit is then derived to account for the effect of training sample size. Monte Carlo experiments compare the theoretical approximations with empirical results under different channel parameters and sample sizes, demonstrating that p+q = 1 constitutes the non-identifiability boundary of the observation channel. The proposed method provides a low-complexity and interpretable statistical tool for XOR key-bit distinguishing in noisy network environments, as well as methodological and theoretical support for key-recovery attacks in practical network scenarios.

title: Development of a Fuzzy Logic Control System for the Noodle Dough Sheeting Process
abstract: The process of dough sheeting is the most crucial step in the production of noodles. In the food industry, the sheeting process of noodle dough is important because it specifically aims to improve the quality and efficiency of noodle production. This study provides a background on the mechanical sheeting process on the mechanical sheeting process used in the food industry, highlighting its significance in shaping, and flattening dough for various goods, particularly noodles. The research identifies several challenges in the current noodle dough sheeting procedures, like uneven dough thickness, surface crack and stickiness. The study formulates a problem statement, emphasizing the need for an accurate and controlled sheeting environment to address these challenges. The proposed solution is to develop and implement a fuzzy logic control system for noodle dough sheeting. The study aims to identify critical parameters influencing dough sheeting and implement fuzzy-rule-base in monitoring the dough sheeting process using identified critical parameters. The amount of flour can be adjusted by the fuzzy control system (software) created in this study, depending on the input parameters, which include surface cracks and dough thickness. The results demonstrated that an ideal dough sheeting method is achieved by implementing a fuzzy system. This research contributes to the advancement of noodle production by introducing a fuzzy logic control system in the development of the dough sheeting process. The findings offer practical insights for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), noodle manufacturers, and sheeting machine manufacturers, paving the way for more efficient and higher-quality noodle production in the culinary sector.

title: Análisis del tiempo de paso en el aprendizaje por refuerzo para robots móviles
abstract: The use of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) in robotics has gained prominence in the last decade, but the impact of its intrinsic temporal components of DRL when applied to physical systems - generally summarized as the timestep duration -, remains underexplored. While some approaches to this issue include timestep duration as part of action space, they offer a limited analysis, overlooking key elements such as software architecture asynchrony or system-induced latencies. These factors cause deviations between nominal and actual timesteps, negatively impacting learning. This article proposes a set of navigation tasks for mobile robots specifically designed to analyze the effects of timestep duration, supported by over 2000 hours of simulation. To our knowledge, this constitutes the first multimetric evaluation of the influence of step time duration on DRL-based robotic tasks. The findings confirm the existence of optimal step times that maximize learning efficiency and task completion.

title: Ensemble deep learning framework for accurate and robust cervical cancer classification
abstract: Early and accurate cervical cancer diagnosis (CCD) is essential for improving treatment outcomes and reducing mortality. However, manual examination of cervical cytology images is labor-intensive, time-consuming, and subject to inter-observer variability. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an ensemble deep learning framework for automated cervical cancer classification. The proposed methodology integrates multiple convolutional neural network (CNN) models to exploit their complementary feature extraction capabilities, thereby improving classification accuracy and robustness. Image preprocessing and data augmentation techniques are employed to enhance image quality, reduce noise, and increase the diversity of the training dataset, enabling better model generalization. The outputs of the individual CNN models are combined through an ensemble decision strategy to generate more reliable diagnostic predictions than those obtained from a single classifier. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms conventional deep learning methods in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). The ensemble approach effectively reduces classification errors while maintaining stable performance across different cervical cell categories. These findings indicate that the proposed framework can serve as a reliable computer-aided diagnostic tool for cervical cancer screening, supporting clinicians in early diagnosis and improving the efficiency, consistency, and reliability of clinical decision making.

title: Hierarchical knowledge graph mapping-guided reinforcement learning planning for space station operations
abstract: Abstract Space station operation planning requires effective coordination among tasks, resources, and execution constraints in a dynamic onboard environment. To transform constraint modeling into reinforcement learning-based decision optimization, this paper maps the Constraint Satisfaction Problem (CSP) model of space station task planning into a Hierarchical Knowledge Graph (HKG) representation and further maps the HKG into a Reinforcement Learning (RL) decision model. Based on this mapping, a CSP-HKG-RL framework is proposed. Through this mapping, task constraints are converted into constraint-aware state and action spaces, and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) is used for final planning optimization. Experimental results show that CSP-HKG-RL reduces invalid action exploration, improves task completion, and generates interpretable scheduling plans.

title: Visual prompt engineering for multimodal and irregularly sampled medical data
abstract: BACKGROUND: A patient undergoes multiple examinations in each hospital stay, where each provides different facets of the health status. These assessments include temporal data with varying sampling rates, discrete single-point measurements, therapeutic interventions such as medication administration, and images. While physicians are able to process and integrate diverse modalities intuitively, neural networks need specific modeling for each modality complicating the training procedure. METHODS: We demonstrate that this complexity can be significantly reduced by visualizing all information as images along with unstructured text and subsequently training a conventional vision-text transformer. Our approach, Vision Transformer for irregular sampled Multi-modal Measurements (ViTiMM), simplifies data preprocessing and modeling by unifying clinical measurements, medications, X-ray images, and electrocardiography scans into a single visual representation. RESULTS: ViTiMM outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in predicting in-hospital mortality, phenotyping, and decompensation on two datasets, the MIMIC-IV and COVID Data for Shared Learning (CDSL) dataset. CONCLUSIONS: We hope our work inspires advancements in multi-modal medical AI by reducing the training complexity to (visual) prompt engineering, thus lowering entry barriers and enabling no-code solutions for training. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/Cardio-AI/ViTiMM .

title: Hybrid BiLSTM-CapsNet for dynamic assessment of entrepreneurship ability in business plans
abstract: Proper assessment of business plan entrepreneurial potential is instrumental in facilitating innovation and stimulating economic growth. However, accurate assessment of unstructured text data within these plans using conventional techniques is extremely difficult. In an effort to transcend these limitations, the current research introduces a novel two-stage deep learning-based approach that incorporates the latest techniques to release more accurate analysis. The methodology designed involves two fundamental steps: first, text feature description and extraction, and second, intelligent classification. In the first step, the Global Vectors for Word Representation (GloVe) approach is used to transform the text into machine-understandable numerical vectors. Thereafter, in the second step, these representations from GloVe are modeled and analyzed through a hybrid Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory-Capsule Neural Network (BiLSTM-CapsNet) model. This hybrid deep learning model, leveraging in turn the advantage of BiLSTM’s sequential modeling and hierarchical modeling abilities of CapsNet along with part-to-whole relationships, enables deep text processing, and the prediction is made on the basis of CapsNet output. The proposed BiLSTM-CapsNet approach was evaluated using a large text dataset, and the results show exceptional performance of the model; its accuracy and F-measure reach 95.70% and 0.9568, respectively. This performance confirms the high capability of the BiLSTM-CapsNet approach in detecting complex patterns and extracting key information from text and proves its improved classification capabilities.

title: HPQEA: A Scalable FPGA‐Based High‐Performance Quantum Emulator With Parallel Architecture and High‐Bandwidth Memory Optimization
abstract: ABSTRACT In recent years, quantum emulation has attracted increasing attention as a practical approach for developing and evaluating quantum algorithms. However, existing solutions often face challenges in achieving broad applicability, high performance, and efficient utilization of hardware resources and memory. To address these limitations, this paper presents the high‐performance quantum emulation accelerator (HPQEA), a hardware architecture based on the state‐vector emulation approach. The proposed design incorporates four key techniques: a strict data storage strategy, a superior flexible processing element network, an optimized and parallelized CX swapper, and a high‐bandwidth memory‐based bulk data transfer engine. Implementation and evaluation on the Alveo U280 FPGA platform demonstrate that HPQEA can emulate quantum circuits efficiently while maintaining high fidelity and low mean square error. Experimental results show that for QFT benchmarks, HPQEA achieves up to 21,093 faster execution than the NVIDIA A100 GPU for circuits with fewer than 20 qubits. Moreover, the comparison with FPGA‐based related works shows promising results with significant speedup in terms of normalize gate speed from 2.77 to 1448.37. In addition, the architecture demonstrates strong energy efficiency, reducing power consumption by up to 15.58 compared to the Intel i9‐10940X CPU and 80.83 compared to the GTX 1080 GPU. These results highlight the scalability, efficiency, and practicality of HPQEA as a hardware platform for accelerating quantum algorithm emulation.

title: Quantum Circuit and Tensor Network Implementation of the 2D Acoustic Wave Equation
abstract: We present a cohesive framework for simulating seismic wave propagation utilizing quantum computing paradigms and their classical tensor network equivalents. We detail a quantum circuit-based formulation for the explicit finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) solution of the two-dimensional acoustic wave equation and map this quantum architecture onto a tensor train representation, namely for Matrix Product State (MPS). The MPS solver enables deterministic simulation of large-scale wavefield dynamics on classical high-performance computing systems. We demonstrate the MPS representation by computing 2D seismic wavefields on the Marmousi model. Our results indicate that the MPS representation is a viable direction for computing and scaling wavefield propagation.

title: Probabilistic Model Checking of Autoregressive Neural Sequence Models
abstract: Test-set accuracy is silent on two issues that matter when deploying autoregressive neural sequence models: how much probability mass the system under test (SUT) places on constraint-violating alternatives that are reachable under sampling and what fraction of the input population satisfies a domain requirement. We answer both with probabilistic model checking. The pipeline extracts a discrete-time Markov chain (DTMC) from the SUT's token-by-token generation, verifies formal PCTL specifications with the PRISM model checker, and aggregates the per-input verdicts into a coverage curve over the input space. A soundness theorem establishes the DTMC as an under-approximation, so every verdict yields a certified interval on the SUT's true reachability probability. The coverage built from those verdicts is, therefore, conservative by construction. A counterexample-guided abstraction refinement (CEGAR) loop adaptively tightens the interval, and a maximum-likelihood algorithm extracts the most probable falsifying trace. Two case studies exercise the pipeline. On a GPT-2 computer-aided process-planning (CAPP) model with 100% test accuracy, the pipeline quantifies the probability mass greedy decoding hides, but that is reachable with sampling; and identifies the smallest training fraction at which an ordering requirement holds population-wide, neither of which test accuracy can report. We then verify the SMILES molecular generator with a 50x larger vocabulary. The only change is an external chemical-validity oracle, and the pipeline identifies the gap between structural completeness and chemical validity.

title: Hardware‐Efficient Hamiltonian Simulation via Trotter‐Initialized Variational Optimization With Native Placement
abstract: ABSTRACT Compiling time‐evolution operators into hardware‐native gate sequences is a bottleneck for digital quantum simulation on noisy intermediate‐scale quantum (NISQ) devices. Generic transpilation treats as an arbitrary unitary, discarding the structure of Hamiltonian dynamics and producing circuits exceeding hardware coherence limits. We introduce a structure‐aware compilation framework that treats product‐formula decompositions as synthesis primitives rather than simulation approximations. The method combines (1) native placement of Hamiltonian terms onto the hardware coupling map, (2) adaptive selection of Trotter blocks via a greedy discretization procedure, and (3) variational refinement using a Trotter‐initialized ansatz. Across Heisenberg, Ising, and XY models with – qubits, compiled circuits achieve fidelities with near‐linear scaling in entangling gates, while generic synthesis produces circuits orders of magnitude deeper. On IBM Torino hardware, shorter approximate circuits outperform deeper exact decompositions: a 27‐CX circuit achieves higher hardware fidelity futher () than a 187‐CX exact circuit. These results demonstrate that structure‐aware approximate compilation outperforms exact structure‐agnostic synthesis, providing a practical pathway for executing Hamiltonian dynamics without pulse‐level control.

title: Calidad frente a cantidad: selecci´on de datasets ontol´ogicos para la generaci´on eficiente de triples en LLMs
abstract: The integration of structured semantic knowledge into Large Language Models (LLMs) is increasingly relevant for knowledge-intensive Natural Language Processing tasks. Ontologies play a central role in organizing this knowledge, yet their manual construction and maintenance become inefficient as digital information grows. While LLMs are increasingly used for ontology learning, their ability to generate coherent structural knowledge remains limited, particularly in small open-source models needed for efficient and sustainable deployment. This work investigates a controlled ontology-to-ontology generation setup to evaluate LLMs’ structural generalization abilities and introduces a data-centric continual pretraining methodology based on ontology quality. Two open-source models, LLaMA 3.2-1B and GEMMA 3-1B, are trained and evaluated using structural and formatting criteria. Results show that selecting only high-quality ontology data substantially improves triple generation while reducing training time by an average of 67% for 1 epoch.

title: Multitask Learning with BERT for Automated Completion of the Breast Cancer Pathology COSD
abstract: Breast cancer pathology reporting is crucial for clinical decision-making and national cancer registration in the UK, and it contributes to the Cancer Outcomes and Services Dataset (COSD). Currently, manual extraction of key variables from free-text reports causes data quality issues and delays. This thesis addresses these challenges by developing a novel Multitask BERT (MT-BERT) framework for automated extraction of structured COSD breast pathology attributes. The proposed model combines a BioMedBERT encoder with specialised classification and regression heads to predict seven variables, including histology, grade, and continuous tumour size. To tackle severe class imbalance and missing labels in a real-world dataset of 7673 reports for 2455 breast cancer patients, the model employs a Round-Robin head-balanced sampling method and a sophisticated loss function. This combines Class-Balanced Cross-Entropy with Label-Distribution-Aware Margins (LDAM) and a center Logit Adjustment technique specifically designed for rare histological subtypes. Evaluated on an independent test set, the MT-BERT achieved a mean Macro-F1 score of 0.5566 across all classification tasks, with laterality reaching production-ready accuracy and other variables, including grade, showing promise, though not yet meeting clinical decision-support thresholds. The performance on minority classes in Histology Coded reached a Macro-F1 of 0.5179, partially validating anti-collapse strategies. For the continuous Tumour Size variable, predictions yielded a MAE of 12.23 mm on the original scale. The framework demonstrates that a unified, data-aware multitask transformer can effectively replicate structured COSD reporting, offering a parameter-efficient approach with a single shared encoder in place of seven separate models to support data completeness within the NHS.

title: Title: Neural Network Architectures for Self-Organized Learning
abstract: This paper explores novel neural network architectures designed to facilitate self-organization and distributed knowledge within a network. Traditional neural networks often struggle with inherent biases and require explicit regularization. We propose a new architecture, termed the "Adaptive Resonance Network" (ARN) variant, that incorporates a dynamically adjusted feedback loop to encourage the creation of complex, self-sustaining patterns. The core mechanism hinges on rewarding networks for producing structures that exhibit low variance – a key characteristic of robust, self-organizing systems. This paper details the design, implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in a simulated learning environment. The focus is on creating networks that can autonomously refine their internal representations, leading to improved generalization and adaptability.

title: Quantum-Inspired Wavefunction Collapse Strategies for Neural Networks
abstract: Quantum-inspired wave function collapse strategies offer a promising avenue for enhancing the convergence and robustness of neural network training. This paper explores the potential of mimicking the collapse of quantum wavefunction states during neural network training, suggesting a novel algorithm that leverages fundamental principles of quantum mechanics to guide the optimization process. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the learning rate based on the predicted wavefunction state, promoting stable and efficient learning. This approach, driven by the concept of quantum entanglement and superposition, has the potential to significantly improve the performance of neural networks across a range of tasks. The paper details the core mechanism, explores preliminary results, and concludes with a discussion of future research directions.

title: Quantum Entanglement Nonlinear Correlation Modeling and Optimization
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents unique challenges for designing and optimizing quantum systems. This paper investigates the modeling and optimization of quantum entanglement using a novel approach that leverages non-linear correlations. We propose a system of optimization algorithms specifically designed to address the limitations of standard optimization techniques, focusing on the inherent properties of entangled states. The core claim is that a model incorporating this non-linear entanglement allows for more precise and efficient control of quantum systems, ultimately leading to enhanced quantum computing performance. This work explores the fundamental principles behind this approach and details the design and implementation of the optimization algorithm.

title: Bushy-tailed Mongoose Metaheuristic Algorithm (BTMMA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Bushy-tailed Mongoose Metaheuristic Algorithm (BTMMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the bushytail mongoose (Suricata suricatta). BTMMA combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) with a unique branching and exploration strategy mimicking the mongoose's efficient search for food. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic branching factor, influenced by the local population density and the objective function value, to guide the search process. A novel 'Foraging Intensity' parameter regulates the exploitation-exploration balance. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a suite of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within a reasonable computational time. The key contributions of this work include the novel branching strategy, the dynamic branching factor, the 'Foraging Intensity' parameter, and a comprehensive evaluation of the algorithm's capabilities. The results indicate that BTMMA is a competitive metaheuristic algorithm with potential applications in various optimization fields. The algorithm's performance is quantified using metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational complexity. Future research will focus on extending BTMMA to handle multi-objective optimization problems and incorporating it into real-world applications.

title: Quantum Entanglement Matrix Adaptive Computation Strategy
abstract: Quantum entanglement matrix (QEM) is a powerful computational paradigm leveraging the unique properties of entangled quantum states. This paper introduces a novel adaptive computation strategy for QEM, designed to exploit the inherent parallelism of quantum computers. We explore a method that dynamically adjusts computational parameters based on the specific quantum circuit being executed, optimizing for increased speed and efficiency. The core mechanism centers around intelligently mapping quantum operations to parallelizable quantum circuits, minimizing the number of quantum gates required and maximizing overall computational throughput. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary results, highlighting its potential to significantly accelerate complex calculations involving QEM.

title: Bristle-faced Free-tailed Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Bristle-faced Free-tailed Bat (BFFB) algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of *Chaereus brachyurus*, commonly known as the bristle-faced free-tailed bat. These bats exhibit a complex and adaptable foraging strategy characterized by erratic flight patterns, rapid changes in direction, and a preference for exploring areas with high food density. The BFFB algorithm leverages these characteristics through a modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) framework. Specifically, the bat's flight patterns are mapped to velocity updates, while the utilization of food patches is modeled through adaptive weight adjustments. The algorithm incorporates a 'whisker' mechanism, mimicking the bat's ability to sense prey, to refine particle positions. Performance evaluations on several benchmark functions demonstrate that the BFFB algorithm achieves competitive results compared to established metaheuristics, particularly in challenging, multimodal landscapes. The algorithm's adaptability and reliance on local exploration and exploitation make it suitable for a range of optimization problems. Key performance indicators, including convergence speed and solution quality, are analyzed. Future research directions include incorporating genetic operators and exploring its application to complex real-world problems.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement Synchronization via Variational Quantum Algorithms
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental resource for quantum computation and communication, offering potential advantages in speed and security. However, maintaining entanglement across multiple qubits poses significant challenges due to decoherence and noise. This paper investigates a novel variational quantum algorithm designed to synchronize entangled states, aiming to surpass current synchronization techniques. The core mechanism relies on a dynamically evolving variational quantum circuit that intelligently adjusts the entanglement state to exceed simple correlations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary experimental results, highlighting its potential to achieve a higher degree of coherence and information transfer compared to existing methods. The algorithm's ability to actively push entanglement beyond simple correlations promises significant advancements in quantum information processing.

title: Bayesian Network Inference and Deep Generative Model Fusion
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for probabilistic modeling and generation by fusing Bayesian Network inference with Deep Generative Models. The core claim is that integrating these two approaches enhances both the accuracy and interpretability of complex dependency modeling. The mechanism relies on leveraging Deep Generative Models to learn and represent prior knowledge in the form of probability distributions, while Bayesian Networks are employed for rigorous inference. We demonstrate that this combined approach addresses limitations inherent in traditional methods, particularly in scenarios with intricate dependencies and a need for explainable AI. The resulting model exhibits improved robustness and allows for a more transparent understanding of the underlying probabilistic relationships. This work represents a significant step towards more reliable and interpretable probabilistic systems.

title: Quantum Metaphor Algorithm for Topological Structure Assessment
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum metaphor algorithm for assessing topological structures of quantum systems. The algorithm leverages the inherent quantum properties of states to evaluate system topology, offering a potential alternative to traditional, classical methods. We present a framework for mapping quantum variables to quantum states, and then utilize these states to determine the topological characteristics of the system. The core mechanism focuses on the interplay between quantum states and the inherent topology of the system, providing a mathematically grounded approach to evaluating design validity. The algorithm demonstrates the ability to identify and quantify topological features, offering a significant advancement in assessing quantum system robustness.

title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning via Causal Decomposition
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved remarkable success in various domains, but its "black box" nature presents a significant challenge. Understanding why an RL agent makes a particular decision is often impossible, hindering trust, safety, and further improvement. This paper introduces Explainable Reinforcement Learning via Causal Decomposition (XRLCD), a novel approach designed to address this opacity. XRLCD decomposes the RL agent's policy into a set of interpretable causal rules. These rules are identified and validated using a causal inference engine, providing a transparent explanation of the agent's decision-making process. The core contribution lies in explicitly modeling the underlying causal reasoning, rather than relying on learned representations, leading to a more understandable and controllable RL system. We demonstrate the effectiveness of XRLCD through a theoretical framework and outline a potential implementation strategy.

title: Title: Topological Structure Dependence Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on topological structure dependence. The core claim is that this algorithm can automatically adjust optimization parameters to adapt to the complexity of topological structures, leading to improved optimization results. The algorithm leverages machine learning to learn the structure of the topological space and dynamically adjust optimization parameters based on this learned structure. The research explores the potential of this approach to overcome limitations of traditional optimization methods, particularly in scenarios involving complex topological spaces. This work aims to provide a robust and automated method for optimizing problems where the topological relationships are significant.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement Dynamics with Variable Coupling Strength
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, exhibits remarkable properties, including instantaneous correlations across vast distances. However, harnessing this phenomenon for practical applications, particularly in quantum computing and quantum communication, remains a significant challenge. The inherent fragility of entanglement – its sensitivity to environmental noise – complicates control and manipulation. This research explores a novel framework for predicting and controlling the evolution of entanglement dynamics, specifically focusing on dynamically adjusted coupling strengths within a quantum system. We introduce a 'resonance' principle – a feedback loop that adapts to the system's internal state – to model this dynamic variability. This approach offers the potential to significantly enhance predictability and control over entanglement, pushing the boundaries of current experimental capabilities. This paper details the theoretical foundation, mathematical modeling, and preliminary experimental validation of this innovative approach, demonstrating its efficacy in predicting entanglement correlations and offering a pathway toward more stable and controllable quantum systems.

title: Nonlinear Geometric Function Models: Adaptive Self-Regulation Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive self-regulation techniques to optimize nonlinear geometric function models. Traditional optimization methods often rely on fixed parameters, while this approach leverages adaptive adjustment to potentially reveal more insightful self-regulating properties. The core aim is to improve model accuracy and efficiency through dynamic parameter adjustments based on the model's inherent characteristics. This work investigates a novel algorithmic framework designed to automatically refine model parameters, achieving superior performance compared to conventional optimization strategies. The research focuses on the concept of self-regulation – the ability of a system to maintain stability and predictability as it evolves – and demonstrates its potential to enhance the robustness and generalization capabilities of complex geometric function models.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Bayesian Inference for Uncertainty Quantification
abstract: Quantum-enhanced Bayesian inference offers a promising approach to address the computational challenges associated with uncertainty quantification, particularly in situations demanding high accuracy and speed. This paper explores the design and implementation of a quantum algorithm, quantum state tomography, to enhance Bayesian inference, aiming to mitigate the inherent cost of traditional methods. We detail the theoretical framework underpinning this approach, highlighting its potential to significantly improve reliability and speed. The core claim centers on leveraging quantum state tomography to achieve a more precise estimate of the system state, thereby bolstering the accuracy of Bayesian inference. This work represents a novel investigation into the application of quantum mechanics to Bayesian inference, with the potential to deliver substantial improvements in computational efficiency and robustness.

title: Efficient and Interpretable Deep State Space Models for Sequence Processing
abstract: Diese Arbeit untersucht, wie Konzepte aus der linearen Regelungstechnik als Entwurfswerkzeug dienen können, um die Effizienz, Interpretierbarkeit und physikalische Realisierung von State Space Models (SSMs) zu verbessern – einer neuen Klasse von neuronalen Netzwerkarchitekturen, die von der Theorie linearer, zeitinvarianter (LTI) dynamischer Systemeinspiriert ist. Obwohl SSMs von der Regelungstechnik inspiriert sind, werden ihre trainierten Parameter selten aus regelungstechnischer Perspektive analysiert oder optimiert. Die vorliegende Arbeit zeigt, dass Eigenwertanalyse, Übertragungsfunktionsdarstellungen und Model Order Reduction (MOR) praktische Werkzeuge über den gesamten Lebenszyklus tiefer SSM-Architekturen hinweg sind – vom Entwurf und Training bis hin zur Komprimierung und physikalischen Realisierung.Wir schlagen S-Edge vor, eine hardwarefreundliche diagonale SSM-Schicht, die Eingabe-, Zustands- und Ausgabedimensionen voneinander entkoppelt und so eine schichtweise Steuerung der Rechenkomplexität ermöglicht. Die zeitkontinuierliche Parametrisierung ermöglicht die Anpassung an unterschiedliche Abtastraten ohne erneutes Training und wird durchschichtweises Downsampling genutzt, um den Inferenzaufwand für die Audioklassifizierung zu reduzieren. Die Eigenwert- und Übertragungsfunktionsanalyse liefert interpretierbare Einblicke in die gelernten Dynamiken, leitet Entscheidungen zum Downsamplingund quantifiziert Diskretisierungseffekte. Die Modelle werden für die Klassifizierung von Roh-Audio Daten und für die Klaviersynthese evaluiert. Auf dieser Grundlage identifiziert die Parameterreduktion nach dem Training mittels MOR-basierter ausgewogener Trunkierung dynamisch redundante Zustände in trainierten SSM-Schichten und ermöglicht so eine strukturierte Komprimierung ohne erneutes Training. Es zeigt sich, dass dasselbe Pruning-Kriterium die Ausdruckskraft zufällig initialisierter linearer rekurrenter Reservoirs verbessert und die hohen Inferenzkosten reduziert, die typischerweise mit dem Reservoir-Computing verbunden sind, während gleichzeitig eine wettbewerbsfähige Leistung bei Benchmarks zur Zeitreihenklassifizierung beibehalten wird. Schließlich werden durch die Auferlegung struktureller Einschränkungen auf diagonale, komplexwertige SSMs zwei Interpretationen etabliert: als parallele Filterbänke zweiter Ordnung mit ausschließlich Polen, die gedämpften oszillierenden Systemen entsprechen, und als lernbare Schichten zur Extraktion von Amplitudenspektrogrammen. Diese Interpretationen verbinden die tiefe SSM-Parametrisierung direkt mit der klassischen Signalverarbeitungslehre und führen zu strukturierten initialisierungsstrategien, die bei Verwendung in einem Reservoir-Computing-Setup zufällige Baselines übertreffen. Durch die weitere Ausweitung dieser physikalischen Verbindung lassen sich gelernte SSM-Dynamiken in der kontinuierlichen Zeit exakt auf analoge elektrische Schaltungen abbilden, was einen konkreten Weg hin zur vollständig analogen Inferenz in neuronalen Netzen aufzeigt.

Durch die weitere Ausweitung dieser physikalischen Verbindung lassen sich gelernte SSM-Dynamiken in der kontinuierlichen Zeit exakt auf analoge elektrische Schaltungen abbilden, was einen konkreten Weg hin zur vollständig analogen Inferenz in neuronalen Netzen aufzeigt.

title: PERBANDINGAN INDOBERT DAN BERT DALAM ANALISIS SENTIMEN KOMENTAR MEDIA SOSIAL TERHADAP PROGRAM MAKAN BERGIZI GRATIS
authors: Irawadi, Irawadi; Pendidikan Agama Islam/Program Pascarjana, Universitas Islam Negri Palopo
abstract: Program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) merupakan salah satu kebijakan pemerintah yang menimbulkan beragam tanggapan publik di media sosial. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis kecenderungan sentimen masyarakat terhadap program MBG serta membandingkan performa model IndoBERT dan BERT Multilingual dalam klasifikasi sentimen. Dataset terdiri dari 3.099 komentar dari TikTok, Instagram, dan X yang diproses melalui tahapan preprocessing, pelabelan sentimen, serta tokenisasi. Evaluasi dilakukan menggunakan metode K-Fold Cross Validation 5-Fold dengan metrik accuracy, precision, recall, dan F1-score. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa IndoBERT memperoleh performa lebih baik dibandingkan BERT Multilingual dengan accuracy sebesar 0,8209% dan F1-score 0,8207%, sedangkan BERT Multilingual memperoleh accuracy 0,8103% dan F1-score 0,8101%. Hasil klasifikasi sentimen menggunakan model terbaik menunjukkan distribusi sebanyak 867 sentimen negatif, 841 sentimen netral, dan 836 sentimen positif. Selain itu, hasil deteksi bahasa menunjukkan bahwa dataset didominasi oleh bahasa Indonesia sebesar 83,35%. Secara keseluruhan, IndoBERT menunjukkan performa yang lebih optimal dan stabil dalam melakukan analisis sentimen terhadap komentar terkait Program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG).

title: Post-Quantum Lightweight Certificateless Hybrid Signcryption Scheme for Time-Series Data Sharing
authors: CHENG Guanjie, SU Taolong, HUANG Junqin, KONG Linghe
abstract: The demand for continuous time-series data sharing in Internet of Things (IoT) scenarios has been increasing. Traditional Certificateless Signcryption (CLSC) schemes based on bilinear pairings or elliptic curves offer limited security under quantum computing threats and incur high computational and communication overheads when repeatedly signcrypting multiple data segments. To address these issues, this paper proposes a post-quantum lightweight certificateless hybrid signcryption scheme tailored for time-series data sharing. First, a bidirectional hash chain-driven symmetric key generation and management mechanism is designed to enable rapid key generation for multiple consecutive data segments while ensuring forward and backward security. Subsequently, a lightweight hybrid signcryption scheme with conditional privacy protection is constructed using a module lattice framework. Combined with an offline/online separation that shifts part of the computation ahead of time, the scheme achieves post-quantum security while significantly reducing the burden on end devices and communication links. The scheme is proven to satisfy IND-CCA confidentiality and EUF-CMA unforgeability in a random oracle model. Prototype implementation and evaluation on resource-constrained terminal devices show that, the proposed scheme achieves significant advantages: on average, the end-side overall latency and transmission volume can be reduced to approximately 40% of those of comparable post-quantum schemes. The advantages of this scheme become even more pronounced in long-duration continuous time-series data scenarios. It effectively balances post-quantum security, lightweight design, and scalability, making it well-suited for time-series data sharing applications in next-generation intelligent IoT.

title: One Algorithm Is Not Enough -Choosing the Right AIML Model for Telecom Fraud Detection
abstract: Telecom fraud has evolved from relatively predictable forms of revenue abuse into increasingly sophisticated attacks involving subscribers, devices, networks, roaming, voice, messaging and digital services. As fraudsters change their behavior, relying on a single machine-learning algorithm is unlikely to provide comprehensive protection. A Random Forest classifier may perform extremely well when historical fraud labels are available. However, the same approach may be less suitable when the objective is to identify previously unseen anomalies, detect sequential behavioral changes, or analyze complex relationships between subscribers, devices, numbers and network entities. This article presents a practical framework for selecting artificial intelligence and machine-learning techniques according to the characteristics of different telecom fraud problems. It examines supervised learning algorithms such as Random Forest, XGBoost and LightGBM; unsupervised techniques such as Isolation Forest; neural-network approaches such as Autoencoders; sequence-based models; and graph-based analytics. The central argument is simple: There is no universal “best” AI algorithm for telecom fraud detection. The appropriate model depends on the fraud type, available data, labeling, behavioral characteristics, temporal patterns, relationships between entities, and operational requirements. A modern fraud management system should therefore be viewed not as a single ML model, but as a portfolio of complementary detection techniques. That is the idea behind my Telecom Fraud AI Benchmark, a practical machine-learning benchmark designed to compare different learning paradigms for telecom fraud detection. The project is available on GitHub: GitHub: https://github.com/adnanmalik83/telecom-fraud-ai-benchmark
